None, live page yuan==its own cash x its own rate) + smoke leg that recomputes from
data/repo_daily/GC001.csv so a forgotten panel refresh reads red.

## E205 A tenor ladder must be rolled on the calendar, not read off the quotes (2026-10-29 r1145 bm-a)

WHEN: a face has to answer "should this cash sit in a longer repo?" and the panels quote
1/3/4/7/14-day legs. E204 priced the 1-day leg; the natural next sentence is "7 days pays
1.35% and 1 day pays 1.09%, so lock it up".

WRONG: compare the quoted rates. They are per annum, and the days actually held are not the
tenor: 1-day money bought on a Friday is lent over the weekend (which is exactly why
Friday's quote dips), while a 3-day leg bought on a Thursday matures on a Sunday and the
cash sits idle until Monday. Comparing quotes would have moved half the capital (528,774)
into GC003, which pays 18.4 bp LESS than rolling the 1-day leg, and into GC007 for a
12.9 bp edge that decays to 5.4 bp at 3 years and 0.4 bp at 5 years.

RIGHT: roll each tenor over the panel's own session calendar, charge rate x calendar-days-
held / 365, reinvest at the first session >= maturity, and PUBLISH the idle days a longer
tenor creates (GC003: 70 days/yr = 19.2% of the calendar; GC007/GC014: 10). Then freeze the
adoption rule as a code constant (edge >= 20 bp in BOTH the 1y and 3y windows, idle <= 1%,
ahead in a majority of complete years) and recompute the verdict from the cells. The first
cut of the message also needed fixing: reporting only the first failing gate blamed GC007 on
"weekend landings" when its real miss was the 20 bp door, and printed "-12.9 bp less" for a
positive edge -- name every failing gate, with sign-preserving wording.

Pos: scripts/etf_book_ceo_page.py cash_ladder()/rolled_yield() (selftest 33->38: flat quotes
adopt nothing, the 1-day leg never idles, +60 bp adopts, +10 bp is rejected by the frozen
door, the live page answers with each tenor's own quote) + the cash-section table in
docs/live_book/LIVE-BOOK-20261029.md + a smoke leg that re-rolls every arm from
data/repo_daily and reds a typed-in verdict.

## E216 A two-lineage merge is a union of *legs*, not a rebase of *commits* (2026-10-29 r1243 bm-b)

Situation: one shared quantitative repo, three hosts, each round adding its own measurement legs
to the same few monster files. Main drifted to 29 local commits vs 38 remote ones because every
round deferred the merge: rebase hangs on this blob:none clone, and mktree replay is banned after a
previous replay silently reverted another machine's ledger.

WRONG: rebase the 29 commits one at a time (29 conflict resolutions, and a rewritten history that
makes the other hosts' verification receipts meaningless), or "resolve by union" at the text level
(`git merge-file --union`). The text union produces a file that will not parse: both sides inserted
complete statements at the same anchor and one side's insert lands *inside* an open list literal
(`_e190_pair = [`), so the merged list closes with the wrong bracket.

RIGHT: merge the two tips with `-c merge.renames=false` (the rename pass is what makes a partial
clone try to lazily fetch objects the promisor remote no longer carries -- `upload-pack: not our
ref`), then resolve by CLASS, never by taste:

  (a) leg containers (main/selftest bodies, smoke leg lists, chain tables): statement-level union
      built on the AST, keep ours' order then theirs' statements not already present, tail return
      last; assert the result parses, compiles, and passes *the file's own selftest*. A green
      selftest is the only proof that nothing upstream was dropped.
  (b) append-only ledgers (card registry, feedback, decision logs): line union, then re-check by
      COUNTING the identities (cards by number) -- "0 lost from either side" is the acceptance,
      not "the file got bigger".
  (c) faces another host is the single writer of: owner-verbatim. Whoever writes them re-derives
      them next round, so taking the owner's copy cannot lose information.

Three things that only show up when you actually run it: two lineages can define the same helper
with different signatures (here `_wide_month_membership`, where each side spells the cash
pseudo-name differently) -- that surfaces as 2 failing legs out of 745, not as a conflict; a
secondary worktree is not a comparable test bed (local untracked inputs such as fleet/machine.json
are absent, and hook-path legs resolve to the worktree admin dir), so its reds must be attributed
before they are believed; and the pre-push size claw is the real guard against the deletion you did
not intend -- the first push was refused for 8 upstream artefacts this lineage had dropped.

Pos: the throwaway-worktree merge recipe (git worktree add --detach + merge -c merge.renames=false +
class-based resolution + ast/py_compile/selftest gates) landed 29 local and 38 remote commits into
one merge commit b768f21763 with ahead 0 / behind 0 and zero files deleted relative to origin.

## E217 A card whose deliverable is already on disk is not open work (2026-10-29 r1244 bm-b)

Situation: results/runnable_pool.json is closed by hand. A round writes the face, the round
report says "burned", and nothing edits the card. Four cards were found sitting at ready/waiting
with their declared deliverable already written — E60-OFFBOOK-LIQUIDITY, E61-SHARED-SUBSET-BOOK,
E64-MIDSWEEP-BURNIN-FACE (198-200h old) and E188-DECOM-LABEL-DUTY (18.9h old) — so the watermark's
"pool ready N" counted finished work as pending work, and the next round was about to burn a card
that needed no burning.

WRONG: read the card's status as the truth about the work, or close cards by eye. Closing by eye
needs a human to re-open four rounds of faces, and the cheap-looking alternative — trust any face
whose name matches the template — closes a card on an older round's output that happens to match.

RIGHT: expand the card's own `deliverable` template (every `<token>` becomes a glob star) and ask
two questions instead of one: does a face exist, and was it written AFTER the card entered? Only
AFTER_ENTRY is evidence that this card was burned; BEFORE_ENTRY is an older round's output wearing
the same name and is reported, never closed. A card with no parsable `entered_at` reads AMBIGUOUS
for the same reason.

Three things only the live run produced:

  (a) the template is not always a filename — E64's deliverable field is
      `results/e44_midmonth/MIDSWEEP-<cutoff>.json (cash_share_pct per era)`, and globbing that
      string verbatim can never match, so the card reads NO_FACE while the face sits on disk under
      exactly the declared name. Strip prose after the first recognised extension and publish
      `declared_prose_stripped` so the reader knows the field was normalised.
  (b) NO_FACE is not the same as "the work did not happen": a card can declare a name and the round
      can ship a different one. List the directory neighbours under the declared literal prefix
      (prefix with trailing punctuation stripped, or `DELIVER-` never matches `DELIVERED-...`),
      restricted to faces newer than entry; disclose, never close.
  (c) closing is only safe as an evidence gate: `apply` flips AFTER_ENTRY cards to done with the
      face as result_ref and is idempotent, so a clean pool costs one glob pass and writes nothing.

Pos: Tools/pool_deliverable_audit.py (check/apply/--selftest, 20/20 legs incl. one leg per wrong
reading above) + results/pool_deliverable_audit.json + wired as the second leg of
Tools/s6_chain_bmb.py so the reconciliation runs before anything that counts "pool ready N".
Live reading: open=4 no_face=0 after_entry=4 -> closed 4, pool ready 0/0 open; the same rule then
re-read the pool as 674 done + 1 ready (E218) after the round seeded its successor card.

## E218 A matched-width control is a distribution, and if its own spread is wider than the gap the split is unresolvable (2026-10-29 r1245 bm-b)

Situation: E61 read the mid-month vs month-end gap (full window +18.0bp) as timing (+84bp) plus
selection (-66bp), but the arm carrying the timing part chose from the month-end book (<=10 names)
while both full arms chose from 1,274 -- so the "selection" part mixed how many names were on offer
with which names were on offer. E218 re-reads the split with both calendars choosing from one seeded
draw of the SAME size, so width is equal and only the decision sessions differ.

WRONG (twice, both caught inside the run): (a) burn ONE matched arm. A same-size draw is a ten-name
book, and its return spread across seeds (402-529bp/yr) is twenty to fifty times the 18bp gap, so a
single draw answers with noise and would have been published as a point estimate. (b) read
"survives" as "|matched| >= 0.5 * |full|". A 20x ENLARGEMENT satisfies that floor, so 2021_2023 was
briefly reported as a survival on a reading 20x the size of the one it was supposed to confirm.

RIGHT: run the control as a distribution (5 seeded draws, seeds published), publish mean AND sd
beside every mean, and ask the resolution question BEFORE the survival question -- if |full| is
inside 2 SE of the control the family is unresolvable at that width, and the face says how many
draws it would take ((2*sd/|full|)^2). Only a resolvable control is then asked to keep sign, keep
half the size, and hold its sign in >=80% of the draws.

Live reading: selection -66.0bp = width +189.4bp (sd 402.4) + pool identity -255.4bp (sd 402.4),
residual 0.0 -- i.e. the -66bp term is the small difference of two terms each about six times its
size and each carrying +-4pp. Calendar: full +18.0bp vs matched -92.4bp (sd 528.9, n=5, SE 236.5,
same-side share 0.4) leads to unresolvable: 3,454 draws would be needed to resolve 18bp. Both
measured eras (2021_2023, 2024_now) are unresolvable too; 2017_2020 is a degenerate cash slice. So
E61's arithmetic identity stands and its two parts are NOT separable at book width 10 by a
random-draw control -- that is the finding, not a survival claim.

Pieces: scripts/e39_panel_census.py modes `sharedbookwidth` + helpers _size_matched_pool /
_width_identity_split / _width_matched_verdict (tri-state: survives / fails / unresolvable) +
constants SHAREDBOOK_WIDTH_{SEED,KEEP,DRAWS,SHARE} echoed into the face; wired as an S6 leg right
after `sharedbook`; a smoke leg pins the face and the chain position. Housekeeping found on the way:
the e39 selftest printed its total BEFORE the last ~50 legs were appended, so the printed count
under-reported while the exit code stayed honest -- the print now sits after the last leg (796/796),
which is why this round's number jumps from the 743 the previous round reported.

## E219 One width is not a measurement of a family: ladder the control and prove the gap is width-invariant before calling a rung a resolution (2026-10-29 r1246 bm-b)

Situation: E218 could not resolve E61's 18bp mid-month vs month-end gap at book width 10 -- a
size-matched seeded control there carries 402-529bp/yr of draw noise, so 3,454 draws would be
needed. A ten-name draw is the noisiest control the book can produce, so the honest follow-up is
not "does the split survive" but "is this family measurable at any width this book actually runs".

WRONG: read the ladder as the same gap measured more finely. It is only that if the gap itself is
width-invariant, and here it is not: the same specification puts the calendar gap at +18.0bp at
pick_n 10, -50.0 at 25, -161.0 at 50 and -45.0 at 100. A "resolved" rung therefore decides only
that rung's number (at width 50 the matched reading is +7.6bp against a -161.0bp gap), and quoting
the narrow rung's 18bp as the quantity being resolved would have been a different question.

RIGHT: (a) burn the SAME seeded size-matched experiment on pick_n = 10/25/50/100, publishing per
rung the control's own sd, the standard error at the draws actually used, and the draws needed to
resolve both the local gap and the frozen reference gap; (b) name the first rung that is resolvable
and re-read the split there, keeping "resolvable" separate from "survives" (a flipped sign at a
resolvable rung is reported as flipped, not as resolved); (c) publish an explicit invariance check
-- gap spread across rungs against the tightest control's standard error -- because without it the
ladder silently licenses reading N different quantities as one.

Live reading (cutoff 2026-10-28, 5 seeded draws per rung, cost x0): control sd 528.9 / 237.3 /
124.8 / 97.3bp (monotone down, as width should), draws needed 3454 / 91 / 3 / 19 -> the family
becomes measurable at pick_n 50 and stops being so at 100 only because the gap shrank to -45.0.
Gap spread 179.0bp vs tightest SE 43.5bp -> gap_is_width_invariant = false. Verdict label
`resolvable_from_width_50`, rung 50 `sign_flips_across_draws`.

Pieces: `scripts/e39_panel_census.py` mode `sharedbookwidthladder` + helpers `_draws_to_resolve` /
`_widthladder_row` / `_gap_width_stability` + constants WIDTHLADDER_{WIDTHS,TARGET_BP}; face
`results/e44_midmonth/WIDTHLADDER-<cutoff>.json`; selftest 796 -> 803 (7 legs: the 3,454 figure
reproduced by the shared formula, narrow/wide/two-target rung readings, frozen constants, and both
directions of the invariance check).

## E220 When a family fails to be width-invariant, split the movement before deciding what to chase -- and here the movement is the calendar part, which is not width-pure either (2026-10-29 r1247 bm-b)

Situation: E219 proved the mid-month calendar gap is not width-invariant (+18/-50/-161/-45bp at
pick_n 10/25/50/100), so the ladder is four numbers rather than one. That leaves the mechanism
open and it is worth closing, because the two readings imply opposite next steps: either the rungs
apply the same calendar offset to different portfolios (the offset's VALUE depends on the book), or
the rungs simply offer different candidate sets (composition). The E61 identity total = timing +
selection decides between them, and it costs nothing to read -- the ladder already publishes both
parts at every rung.

WRONG: assume the movement must be selection, because width is what changes which names are on
offer. That story is intuitive and it is not what the numbers say: selection stays inside
-66..+33bp across all four rungs (range 99bp) while timing runs +84 / -83 / -188 / -3 (range
272bp). The part that moves is the part that was supposed to be calendar-pure.

RIGHT: (a) read timing as total - selection at every rung, and carry the identity flag per rung
rather than trusting the subtraction silently; (b) attribute each rung STEP, not the endpoints --
"timing agrees with the total in 3/3 steps, selection opposes in 2/3" is a different statement
from "timing is bigger at the ends"; (c) run the SAME invariance test on the part that carries the
movement (272bp spread against the 43.5bp tightest standard error), so "the movement is timing"
cannot be read as "the calendar effect is stable".

Live reading (cutoff 2026-10-28, cost x0): timing 84.0/-83.0/-188.0/-3.0, selection
-66.0/+33.0/+27.0/-42.0, total 18.0/-50.0/-161.0/-45.0; timing range 272.0 against selection range
99.0; tightest SE 43.5 -> `timing_carries_movement_without_a_width_invariant_number`. Consequence:
the mid-month calendar question closes with no quotable number at any width -- E61/E218/E219/E220
leave the effect as a per-width reading only.

Pieces: `scripts/e39_panel_census.py` mode `sharedbookwidthsplit` + helpers `_widthsplit_rows` /
`_widthsplit_range` / `_widthsplit_movement` / `_widthsplit_verdict` + constant
`WIDTHSPLIT_TOL_BP`; face `results/e44_midmonth/WIDTHSPLIT-<cutoff>.json`; S6 leg right after
`sharedbookwidthladder`; a smoke leg pins the face, the chain position and that every rung carries
both parts; selftest 803 -> 812 (9 legs: the identity at both ends, a rung with no selection term,
3/3 timing agreement, 2/3 selection opposition, both ranges, the label, the invariance direction,
and a single-rung face that must say insufficient_rungs).

### E221 — for a calendar effect the sample size is MONTHS, not names (r1248 bm-b)

The mid-month family (E61/E215/E218/E219/E220) closed with no quotable number at any
width because a ten-name book's draw noise is 20-50x the 18bp it had to explain. The
cheap version of the same question, asked over the whole ETF universe (1,725 names x
5,268 sessions, 3,786 scored cross-sections, median 148 names/session), produces the
rule and the number at once.

Rule: **a calendar effect is observed once per month, so widening the cross-section buys
no power.** From 5 names to 1,725 changed nothing about resolvability because the
independent observation is the month. Live reading (cutoff 2026-10-28, close-to-close,
equal weight, no costs): unconditional +2.20bp/session; month-end last-two +8.31bp vs
rest-of-month +3.91bp -> gap +4.40bp at SE 6.84, t=0.64. The power block names the price
of settling it: 3,567 months (~297 years) for a 4.40bp gap at 80% power. So E219's
"unresolvable at matched width" is a property of calendar questions on a 14-year panel,
not a defect of the book.

Shape finding: the mass sits on the TURN of the month, not on a two-day "month-end"
bucket -- last session +19.20bp (t 2.13 over 188 months) against a -2.58bp penultimate,
first session +27.47bp (t 2.69), turn-of-month group +23.32bp (t 3.43). The best single
cell is below the ladder's own 23-bucket bar (3.07, so `clears_bonferroni=false`), and
the turn-of-month group that does clear it was formed after seeing the ladder -- a
pre-registerable candidate, not a finding.

Statistical rule worth keeping: the standard error must be over SESSIONS. Inside one
session all ETFs move together, so a name-day SE would read ~0 and call a gap that
cancels to zero across months infinitely significant; a fixture with identical moves per
session and opposite-sign month-ends pins this.

Pieces: `scripts/e221_dom_profile.py` (`run` / `selftest`, 18 hermetic legs); face
`results/dom_profile/PROFILE-<cutoff>.json` + `by_dom.csv`; S6 leg `dom_profile` right
after `sharedbookwidthsplit`; a smoke leg that recomputes the published gap from the
published group stats and fails if the power block, the multiple-comparison bar or the
coverage count disappears. Pit caught in-window: testing `se_bp` for truthiness reported
"insufficient_days" for a perfectly measured 100bp gap (a zero-variance group has se ==
0.0) -- test against None.

### E222 — a post-hoc shape is not a rule until it pays the toll (r1249 bm-b)

E221 shipped the turn-of-month shape as a candidate. E222 is the cheap test that turns a
candidate into a verdict: same calendar shape, one tradable instrument, costs, an IS/OOS
split frozen before reading, and a decision rule that lives in code and is echoed on the
face so a gate can reject a mismatch.

Rule: **one round trip per month.** Holding a month's first and last session is a
contiguous hold across the boundary (last of M is adjacent to first of M+1), so the toll
is 2 sides at 13.041bp = 26.08bp/month, not 2 sides per held session. Getting that wrong
doubles the cost and manufactures a REJECT.

Reading (sh510300, 173 months to 2026-10-28, IS 103 / OOS 70): overlay nets +262.1bp/yr
on 9.9% time in market against 554.0bp/yr for buy-and-hold -> excess -291.9bp/yr full
sample, but IS -65.1bp/mo and OOS +35.7bp/mo. The sign disagrees across the split, OOS
t=0.65 against a 2.39 bar, and the price of settling it is 1,317 months (~109.7 years)
at 80% power. Verdict REJECT on all three variants, single instrument and basket alike.

Two statistical rules come out of it. (1) A calendar rule is observed once per MONTH, so
widening from 1 ETF to 5 moved the excess by 1.5x and the t from 0.65 to 0.36 -- noise,
not resolution; history is the only currency and this instrument has 173 months of it.
(2) A sign flip across IS/OOS is not a boundary case to argue about, it is two samples
of noise.

Pieces: `scripts/e222_tom_overlay.py` (`run` / `selftest`, 24 hermetic legs); face
`results/tom_overlay/TOMO-<cutoff>.json` + `latest.json`; S6 leg `tom_overlay` after
`dom_profile`; smoke leg recomputing the excess identity and rejecting an ADOPT that
never cleared the bar. Pits: a zero-variance fixture makes REJECT unreachable (se==0 ->
`oos_series_unusable`; assert dispersion first, r1261 family); filtering unpriced months
inside the arm instead of before the split reads OOS one month short against its floor;
month boundaries are session-adjacent by construction, so the face publishes
`single_session_months` instead of a vacuous adjacency check.


### E223 — more observations are not more resolution (r1250 bm-b)

E222 rejected the turn-of-month overlay and priced the question at ~110 years, because a
calendar rule is observed once a month. The tempting successor is a faster anchor. E223
tests that directly: the same accounting on a ladder of anchors -- month turn (12/yr) and
three weekly ones holding the first 1/2/3 sessions of each ISO week (52/yr) -- one round
trip per PERIOD, frozen IS/OOS, decision rule in code.

Result on sh510300 (3,503 sessions to 2026-10-28): monthly +428.97bp/yr excess at t=0.65
(MDE 1,860.6bp/yr); weekly -1,100.6 / -1,239.2 / -1,255.7bp/yr at t=-1.63 / -2.38 / -2.79
(MDE 1,888.2 / 1,461.9 / 1,261.1). All four REJECT, and the ladder's answer is the
comparison: 4.3x the observations buys 0.68x-1.01x the annual resolution.

The rule this card exists for: resolution is set by sd_per_period * sqrt(periods_per_year),
not by the observation count. MDE_ann = z*sd*sqrt(per_year/years); shortening the holding
window shrinks the per-period signal and its dispersion together, so the annual bar barely
moves -- and the highest-frequency / thinnest rung can be strictly WORSE than the slow one
(here week_h1 1,888 vs the monthly 1,861). A rejected calendar rule's successor must raise
the number of *independent* observations without cutting exposure per observation; a faster
calendar rule pays the toll more often and buys nothing.

Pieces: scripts/e223_obs_rate_ladder.py (
un / selftest, 26 hermetic legs); face

esults/obs_rate/OBSRATE-<cutoff>.json + latest.json; S6 leg obs_rate_ladder after
	om_overlay; smoke leg that re-derives every rung's MDE from its own dispersion and fails
a rung that ADOPTs below the bar. Pit: the ladder summary needs all four rungs in its
fixture or it raises instead of reporting a short ladder; and a bp fixture written in
percent units asserts 100 when the truth is 1000.

### E224 -- the observation wall is set by the hold, not by the sampling rate (r1251 bm-b)

E223 rejected a faster calendar anchor and named the successor it wanted: a rule whose
independent observations rise without cutting the exposure per observation -- a
continuously-sampled state gate. E224 tests that with four volatility arms (trailing
20-session vol in the bottom/top tercile of its own previous 250 values) x hold 10/20
sessions, entry at the close of the qualifying session, one round trip per EPISODE, the
gate not polled while holding so episodes are disjoint.

Result on sh510300 (3,503 sessions to 2026-10-28): all four primary arms and all four
basket arms REJECT; OOS excess -377 to -836bp/yr (t -0.65 to -1.92), the positive basket
arms at +0.3/+31.3 dying at x2 costs.

The rule this card exists for: **a continuously-sampled signal does not produce continuous
observations**. A hold of H sessions caps the episode count at 252/H, and the gate fills
only part of that cap -- at H=10 the ceiling is 25.2/yr and the gate reached 10.5 (41.7%),
i.e. BELOW the 12/yr a monthly calendar anchor gets for free. So "sample more often" is
the wrong lever in both directions: E223 showed a shorter hold pays the toll more often,
E224 shows a state gate still pays per episode and gains its resolution only from
sd_per_episode (810.7 vs 1,860.6 bp/yr = 2.30x tighter with half the observations).

Sister rule (published beside it): the overlapping-day reading does NOT inflate here --
naive per-day t is 0.31-0.88x the episode-level t, because days inside one hold are less
dispersed than independent draws. Episodes are the honest unit because the days are
dependent, not because pooling them manufactures significance. Every such face must
publish episodes/yr beside the 252/H ceiling it is drawing on, and naive_days must equal
episodes x hold.

Pieces: scripts/e224_vol_gate.py (run / selftest, 18 hermetic legs); face
results/vol_gate/VOLGATE-<cutoff>.json + latest.json + by_arm csv; S6 leg vol_gate after
obs_rate_ladder; smoke leg re-derives each MDE from its own dispersion, checks the toll is
one round trip, refuses an episode rate above 252/H and a naive day count that is not
episodes x hold. Pit: a mean indistinguishable from zero produced years_needed = 3e5..1e8,
which reads as a measurement -- now suppressed to null with years_needed_unbounded = true.


### E225 -- a continuous weight buys sessions, not resolution; their payoff is not the gate's (r1252 bm-b)

E224 ended on a cap: a hold of H sessions limits a gate to 252/H independent episodes a
year, so no sampling rate can raise the count. Its named successor was the one design the
accounting does not throttle -- a weight that varies continuously with the state, decided
at every close, with no per-episode round trip. E225 prices that on the SAME signal and the
SAME toll: trailing 20-session vol, tercile thresholds from its own previous 250 values,
unit turnover |dw| pays 13.041bp, decision at the close of t applies to the return of t+1.

Result on sh510300 (3,503 sessions to 2026-10-28, 1,401 OOS decisions): 0 of 5 arms adopt.
The load-bearing number is not the verdict, it is that the sample is nearly independent:
n_eff/sessions = 97% (1,363 of 1,401), so daily reweighting genuinely escapes E224's
episode cap -- and the annual bar still lands at 1,006bp/yr against the episode-locked
gate's 811bp/yr, a 0.81x move in the WRONG direction. More independent observations, worse
annual resolution. Why: a weight between 0 and 1 spreads the same signal over more
observations at lower amplitude, so per-observation dispersion falls by less than the count
grows, and the toll is charged per unit of weight change (11.0 round-trip units a year for
binary_low, 199bp/yr of cost) -- a cost the episode lock pays once per hold instead.

The second rule is the one that keeps a negative result readable: **the null arm already
prices the drift, so a gated arm's excess is not a verdict on the gate**. always_on (w=1,
no turnover) reads -1,628bp/yr on the OOS window: that is the out-of-sample drift sitting
below the in-sample drift the face normalises to, not a property of gating. Charging every
arm that deficit in proportion to its average exposure leaves the gate-specific residual:
binary_low -524, tilt_step -637, tilt_linear -704, voltarget -200 bp/yr -- so the tilt
genuinely lost money beyond the drift, and the smallest loss (voltarget, 93.5% exposure,
2.8 turnover/yr) is the arm that traded least, not the one that timed best.

How to apply: any continuously-held overlay must publish (a) n_eff beside its session count
or "more data" is an assumption, (b) the null arm's excess as the drift deficit, and (c)
gate_specific = excess - avg_weight x null_excess, or a market-wide drift miss gets read as
a verdict on the rule. Pieces: scripts/e225_state_tilt.py (run / selftest, 18 hermetic
legs); face results/state_tilt/TILT-<cutoff>.json + latest.json + by_arm csv; S6 leg
state_tilt after vol_gate; smoke leg re-derives each MDE from z*se_nw*252, refuses n_eff >
n, and refuses a drift split that does not re-add. Pit: a HAC leg whose fixture is a
sawtooth carries negative lag-1 correlation and fails the "NW >= iid" assertion the method
needs -- the fixture noise must be white (LCG) before that leg means anything.

### E227 -- a break-even toll is a property of the line, and clearing a toll is not clearing a bar (r1253 bm-b)

E225 left one arithmetic question open and it did not need a new study. Its gate-specific
residual runs on a per-unit-turnover toll, so in the cost `c` it is a straight line:

    gate_specific(c) = gate_specific(0) - c * D,   D = arm turnover/yr - avg_w * null turnover/yr

One root, `c* = gate_specific(0) / D`, in bp per unit of turnover. The sweep (0 -> 3x the
frozen 13.041bp) is the evidence and the closed form is the answer; they are asserted equal
to 4.5e-13 bp/yr, and the root re-evaluated through the engine reads 1.1e-13.

Result. On sh510300 (3,503 sessions to 2026-10-28, 1,401 OOS decisions) every gated arm is
DEAD AT ANY PRICE: the largest gross gate-specific residual (voltarget) is -174 bp/yr before
paying anything, and the highest break-even belongs to a DIFFERENT arm (binary_low, -21.2
bp/unit) -- a negative cost would be needed, i.e. the gross rule loses before it trades. All
four gated arms share that state. On the equal-weight basket one root does land above the
model cost (binary_low, 36.5 bp/unit), and that is exactly where the second rule earns its
keep: at 13.041bp that arm's excess is +1.8 bp/yr at t=0.01. It survives the toll by standing
at ZERO, after a null arm that lost -662 bp/yr -- its +340 bp/yr gate-specific residual is
the drift attribution, not money the tilt earned. 0 of 1 survivors clear the bar.

**Ranking by residual and ranking by break-even name different arms** once every arm is
below zero. The first version of this face printed "the best gate-specific arm (binary_low)
stands at -324 bp/yr": binary_low has the highest ROOT, voltarget the highest residual.
Publish both selectors separately (`best_gate_specific_arm` / `best_break_even_arm`) and
have a selftest leg feed a fixture where they disagree -- a label picked by one criterion and
written as the other is how a face lies with every number correct.

How to apply:
1. When an arm's residual is linear in a cost, publish the ROOT rather than only the
   verdict at one cost -- and publish the ladder so the line is visible.
2. Always read a "survives the cost" verdict again at that cost, with its t beside its
   annual excess. Toll survival and statistical survival are different claims and a face
   that prints only the first will be read as the second.
3. Publish 1/D as root fragility: voltarget pays only 2.0 units/yr on the single panel, so
   100bp/yr of measurement error moves its root 50 bp/unit. A flat line makes the root a
   wild extrapolation even when the arithmetic is exact.
4. **Do not assert an ORDERING between two roots whose direction depends on the sign of an
   intercept.** gate_specific(c) and excess(c) differ by avg_w * null_excess, constant in c,
   so which root is larger flips with the sign of the null arm's drift. My first leg
   asserted "the excess-basis root is stricter" and failed on a negative root -- the fix is
   to assert the IDENTITY `excess_root - gate_root == avg_w * null_excess / D`, which holds
   whichever way the signs fall (measured 22.2140 vs expected 22.2140 bp/unit).

Pieces: scripts/e226_tilt_breakeven.py (run / selftest, 18 hermetic legs); face
results/state_tilt/BREAKEVEN-<cutoff>.json + breakeven_latest.json + breakeven_by_arm csv;
S6 leg tilt_breakeven immediately after state_tilt; smoke leg re-derives every published
root from its own line (c**D == g0), refuses a root published without a positive toll
differential, refuses a sweep that rises with cost, and refuses a survivor recorded with no
excess read at that cost.

### E228 -- an attributed share of the null's drift is already an exposure-matched benchmark, and what it lacks is an error bar (r1254 bm-b)

E226 flagged the drift split as unsafe: on the equal-weight basket `binary_low` carried
+340 bp/yr of `gate_specific` beside +1.8 bp/yr of real excess, so the split looked able to
hand a losing rule a positive residual. E228 replaced it with a TRADED benchmark -- a flat arm
at the gated arm's own average weight, same `mu_is`, same |dw| x 13.041bp toll, w_{-1}=0 --
and judged the PAIRED daily difference `excess_gated - excess_matched` with a Newey-West t.

The answer is structural, and it is the opposite of the worry: on all 8 gated cells
(4 arms x 2 panels) the attribution and the traded benchmark differ by **0.0 bp/yr**, so
**0 of 8 arms change sign**. The identity is exact --
`attribution - pair == -(matched arm's own out-of-sample toll)` -- and a constant weight
trades only at entry, so that toll is **exactly 0.0**. An attributed share of the null's drift
IS the exposure-matched benchmark whenever the null stops trading after entry. What the
published residual lacked was never bias, it was a STANDARD ERROR: the split printed a point
estimate with no dispersion, and the paired series is what supplies one.

Measured (sh510300, 3,503 sessions to 2026-10-28; basket 5,268 sessions; bar 2.7344 =
Bonferroni over 4 arms x 2 panels): 0 of 8 cells survive. Best case for the tilt is the
basket's binary_low at +218 bp/yr, t=0.71, MDE 857 bp/yr; the single panel's four arms run
-524/-637/-704/-200 bp/yr at t -1.69..-2.15. The E226 +340.08 was the zero-cost reading of
the same cell; the 121.66 bp/yr drop to +218.42 equals the gate's own OOS toll (121.658)
exactly, which is the price of being measured.

How to apply:
1. When you publish a "what the rule itself earned" residual, ask whether a traded arm exists
   that holds the same exposure. If it does, price it and publish the PAIR -- the pair cancels
   the drift term and therefore has a usable standard error, which an attribution never has.
2. Publish the identity that makes the two agree, not just the agreement. `0 of N sign
   changes` reads as an empirical result that could break next quarter; the identity says
   exactly where it would break -- any benchmark that REBALANCES (the moment the null arm
   trades after entry, its toll stops being zero and the two numbers separate).
3. Two matched constants answer two questions and must both be printed: the IS-frozen one is
   the only causal benchmark; the OOS one is an exact exposure match that looks at the answer.
   Their difference is predictable, not noise -- a post-split drift shift of k moves the pair
   by `k * (avg_w_oos - c_is) * 252` under the frozen constant and by exactly 0 under the
   matched one (76.3636 vs 76.3636 measured).

Pieces: scripts/e228_matched_exposure.py (run / selftest, 22 hermetic legs); face
results/state_tilt/MATCHED-<cutoff>.json + matched_latest.json + matched_by_arm csv; S6 leg
matched_exposure immediately after tilt_breakeven; smoke leg re-derives every paired MDE from
its own SE, refuses a matched arm that trades more than its entry side, and refuses an
attribution gap that is not the matched toll.

### E229 -- split the pair before you explain it: which days, how much, and the toll (r1255 bm-b)

E228 gave the paired timing value a standard error but never asked where it comes from. The
question a reader actually has is binary: is the gate unable to time, or does it pick the
right days and size them wrong? That question is arithmetic on a series already on disk.

The identity (c = the gated arm's own OOS average weight, mu_is = the drift every arm is
charged, per OOS session t):

    d_t = (w_t - c)(r_t - mu_is) - cost_t
        = 1[w_t = 0]*(-c)(r_t - mu_is)          selection -- which days
        + 1[w_t > 0]*(w_t - c)(r_t - mu_is)     sizing    -- how much
        - cost_t                                toll

and sizing splits exactly into LEVEL (`n_in*m_w*m_r`, the in-market average weight sitting
away from c) and COVARIANCE (holding more when the return is above the drift). All three
reconstruct the pair to 2.0e-12 bp on every cell, so no channel can drift away from the
series it claims to explain.

Measured (sh510300 1,402 OOS sessions to 2026-10-29, basket 2,108; bar_arm 2.734,
bar_channel 3.078 = Bonferroni over 4 arms x 2 panels x 3 channels):
* `binary_low` is the only gate that dodges the right days -- the sessions it sits out
  average -4.61 bp (single) / -4.79 bp (basket) against the drift, giving selection
  +261 / +265 bp/yr, but at t=1.26 / 1.32 it is nowhere near the bar. E228's one positive
  cell (was +218 bp/yr, now +227) is a right-signed, unresolved SELECTION effect, not sizing skill.
* `tilt_step`/`tilt_linear` sit out sessions averaging +0.72 / +1.76 bp ABOVE the drift --
  a long-only gate stepping aside above the mean, exactly backwards.
* the only channel that clears the bar is the TOLL (tilt_* on the basket, t=-10.03, -10.05).
  What separates these arms from a flat constant is measurably the cost of moving.
* a 0/1 gate cannot have a sizing channel: `binary_low`'s covariance term is identically
  zero (max 6.8e-28 bp/yr), so its whole sizing channel is a level shift. Any "sizing skill"
  claimed for a binary rule is arithmetically impossible.

How to apply:
1. When a paired/level statistic is unexplained, look for an identity that partitions it
   into named channels before running anything new. The partition is free and it converts
   one number into a sentence a reader can act on.
2. Align constructions on the RETURN index, not the weight index: the weight set at i
   covers the return at i+1, so "sit out session j" is w[j-1]=0. Two construction legs
   failed on exactly that off-by-one (and an in-sample dodge also moves mu_is, so only OOS
   sessions are dodgeable when manufacturing a channel).
3. Publish the structural zeros. A channel that is identically zero for a family of rules
   (binary gate -> no covariance) is a stronger statement than a measured zero, and it
   forecloses a whole class of future claims.

Pieces: scripts/e229_timing_selection.py (run / selftest, 16 hermetic legs); face
results/state_tilt/TIMINGSEL-<cutoff>.json + timingsel_latest.json + timingsel_by_arm csv;
S6 leg timing_selection immediately after matched_exposure; smoke leg re-adds the published
channels, refuses a face whose parts do not reconstruct its own pair, and refuses a binary
arm that publishes a covariance.


### E230 -- the toll is buyable, but the buy rarely pays for itself (r1256 bm-b)

E229 established that the only channel separating these gated rules from a flat constant is
the TOLL (t ~ -10 on the basket). The toll is charged on |dw|, so the next question is
mechanical: can a hysteresis deadband on the same volatility signal buy it back? A five-rung
ladder (0, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 1.00, 2.00 x in-sample sd of the signal), three arms, two
panels, x1 and x2 costs, answered it: the band removes 36-1,138 weight changes per cell and
the toll falls by +81..+399 bp/yr -- but only 1 of 30 cells clears a Bonferroni bar of 3.34
on the PAIRED delta, 5 lose to the base arm and 24 are point-estimate-only.

What to keep:

* **A mechanical saving is not a paid-for improvement.** Every rung saved toll; almost none
  of them improved the pair enough to resolve. The selection channel gave back -243..+290
  bp/yr of the same order. Report the saving and the bar together or the saving reads as a
  result.
* **A rule that stops trading is not a rule that trades cheaply.** At the widest bands 6 of
  30 cells sat at or below 5 weight changes over the whole sample: the band had replaced the
  arm with a buy-and-hold at roughly the base exposure -- the null arm. Any toll saving
  there is the null's zero turnover. Publish a collapse floor and refuse a PAYS verdict on a
  collapsed rung (smoke leg enforces it); this is the difference between "the rule got
  cheaper" and "the rule left".
* **Freeze one constant when you ladder.** E229's per-arm exposure match re-derives the
  constant from each arm's own OOS average weight; applied per rung, every rung would have
  its own benchmark and the rungs would not be comparable. Fix c at the base arm, and the
  identity pair = selection + sizing + toll still holds for any c.
* **Print the identities that make a gate look strong.** The toll is exactly linear in the
  cost parameter, so d_toll(x2) == 2*d_toll(x1) identically and the x2 limb of any "still
  pays at double cost" condition is mechanically weaker than the x1 limb. A selftest leg
  pins the factor of two so the disclosure cannot drift.
* **The base rung has to be the thing the ladder is about.** band = 0 must reproduce E225's
  weights series exactly (asserted per arm, not tested once), and the published base numbers
  must equal E229's to the decimal -- otherwise the ladder's origin is a lookalike.

How to apply:
1. Before declaring a "cost fix", ask whether the rule still exists at the setting that
   produced it; if the change count collapsed, the fix is the null arm.
2. Ladder one knob at a time against a frozen benchmark, and put the bar on the paired
   difference, not on either level.
3. Write the mechanical scale identities (toll ~ cost) into the face as disclosures with a
   selftest pin, so the face cannot later claim them as findings.

Pieces: scripts/e230_hysteresis_toll.py (run / selftest, 15 hermetic legs); face
results/state_tilt/HYSTERESIS-<cutoff>.json + hysteresis_latest.json + hysteresis_by_rung
csv; S6 leg hysteresis_toll after timing_selection; smoke leg re-adds each rung's split,
refuses a fix under the bar or on a collapsed rule, and requires a rung-0 baseline per arm.

### E231 -- a path test answers with a share, and the families must stay apart (r1257 bm-b)

E230 left one of thirty cells above its bar, at the smallest band in the grid. Re-measuring
that grid on 25 panel-paths (split offsets, execution lags, calendar eras) separates three
facts that a single cell conflates: the SIGN is robust (12/12 paths positive), the SIZE is
not (8/12 clear the bar; lags 2-3 miss), and the MAGNITUDE is a full-sample artefact (inside
either era the improvement shrinks ~3.5x to 77-81 bp/yr at t 1.4-1.8 and cannot resolve).
Zero of 48 cells survive every path.

Three rules:
1. Report the share of paths that keep the sign AND the share that clear the bar. They are
   different claims; printing only the first reads as a confirmation.
2. Never merge path families into one range. Moving the split/lag re-measures one sample;
   re-deriving inside an era is a different experiment. Merged, the median is the
   full-sample number and it stands in for a statement about a period. Publish the families
   apart and pin the separation in a selftest leg.
3. Give the arm the weaker bar deliberately -- reuse the previous study's frozen bar rather
   than deriving one that fits this sweep, so the rejection is a line the arm was already
   granted. Publish the strict bar beside it without letting it rescue anything.

Pieces: scripts/e231_band_path_test.py (run / selftest, 18 hermetic legs); face
results/state_tilt/BANDPATH-<cutoff>.json + bandpath_latest.json + bandpath_by_cell csv;
S6 leg band_path_test after hysteresis_toll; smoke leg cross-replays the global path against
E230's published cell (1e-6 bp / 1e-9 t), refuses a survivor without a clean sweep, and keeps
the two path families from being merged.

### E232 -- a cost model is a design choice, so every conclusion through it owes a curvature sweep (r1258 bm-b)

E226-E231 all charge |dw| at a fixed 13.041 bp/side, which makes every toll number in the
family a fact about a LINEAR charge. Sweeping gamma in 0.75/1.00/1.25/1.50 with the unit cost
of a full 1.0 move held fixed answers the question in three parts: the toll clears its bar on
6/6 arm cells at every gamma and stays the ONLY channel past it (so the family's conclusion is
curvature-invariant), the toll's SIZE is not (-247.3 -> -93.2 bp/yr on tilt_linear, a 2.6x
erosion taking the pair from -788.1 to -634.0), and E230's single passing band dies: BAND_PAYS
at gamma <= 1.00, BAND_NOISE at 1.25/1.50, ladder counts 2/1/0/0.

Three rules:
1. Parameterise the charge and hold the price of one full move fixed across the sweep. Then
   require the SIGN of a claimed channel to survive every point before its magnitude is
   discussed -- significance and size answer different questions.
2. Discrete rules are degenerate cases of graded ones. A 0/1 gate only moves whole units and
   1**gamma == 1, so its toll cannot respond to curvature at all (binary_low is flat to 1e-9
   at four gammas and carries the family's only positive pair cell). Flag that as an invariant;
   never read the gate's flatness as robustness.
3. Selection and sizing never touch the charge, so they are the control:
   pair(g) - pair(g') == toll(g) - toll(g'). Pin it in a selftest and no cross-gamma move in
   the pair can later be re-narrated as skill.

Sibling: a study ticket can carry an inverted premise and the face must measure the direction
rather than repeat it -- the card claimed a concave charge makes many small steps cheaper per
unit, and 0.5**0.75 = 0.594 > 0.5 is the opposite.

Pieces: scripts/e232_cost_curvature.py (run / selftest, 10 hermetic legs); face
results/state_tilt/COSTCURVE-<cutoff>.json + costcurve_latest.json; S6 leg cost_curvature after
band_path_test; smoke leg requires >=3 gamma points, selection invariant on every arm cell,
binary_low's toll unmoved across gammas, and a re-read of E230's focus cell.

### E233 -- a swept parameter is still an assumed one; measure it, then publish the identification span (r1259 bm-b)

E232 read the family under gamma = 0.75/1.00/1.25/1.50 -- four points nobody calibrated, while
the production charge (13.041 bp/side on |dw|) is gamma = 1.0 by construction. Estimating the
exponent from the panel itself (`|r_oc| = k * amount ** gamma`, HAC interval, era split)
returns 0.928 [0.830, 1.026] on sh510300 and 0.917 on the basket, pre-2017 1.079 / 2017+ 0.883:
the assumption was inside the measurement, and E232's headline erosion is real but far smaller
at the measured exponent (toll -217.3/-187.3/-163.0 bp/yr over the interval, i.e. ~16% lost
across the path, not 2.6x). The toll clears its bar on 6/6 arm cells at every point.

Three rules:
1. **The sampling interval is not the uncertainty.** One control set (same panel, same estimator
   family) moves gamma from 0.928 to 0.255 and the intervals are disjoint; on the basket the
   naive reading collapses to 0.003. Publish the identification span as an explicit point set
   and re-derive every verdict inside it -- otherwise "gamma is known to +/- 0.10" is a claim
   about the regression, not about the number.
2. **A reverse regression's reciprocal is not the forward elasticity.** Publish the reverse fit
   (amount on |r|) as a diagnostic, fence it in code so it can never be read as an estimate,
   and pin that with a selftest leg: 1/0.169 = 5.9 is an object with no interpretation.
3. **Fence the bridge in prose on the face itself.** What is measured is the market's elasticity
   of price to aggregate turnover; using it as our own |dw| exponent assumes the traded amount
   is proportional to |dw| and that our flow meets the same concavity. `frozen_spec.bridge`
   carries that sentence and the smoke leg refuses a face without it.

Sibling findings worth carrying: E230's one passing band is BAND_PAYS on the fine scan from
gamma 0.25 all the way to 1.10, so it is not a curvature artefact inside the measured range
(its limit is path fragility, E231: 12/12 positive, 4/12 clearing the strict bar); and 3 of 12
ladder cells flip only at the naive gamma, all in the same direction -- counted, printed, not
left for a reader to find.

Pit: a constant regressor does not make X'X singular in floats (`1e8` columns invert to
garbage and yield a confident gamma), so the collinearity guard must be scale aware -- test the
determinant of the correlation form, not of the raw cross-product.

Pieces: scripts/e233_empirical_gamma.py (run / selftest, 13 hermetic legs); face
results/state_tilt/EMPIRICAL-GAMMA-<cutoff>.json + empirical_gamma_latest.json; S6 leg
empirical_gamma after cost_curvature; smoke leg requires a published interval containing the
point estimate, the interval endpoints among the re-derived points, a surviving toll channel,
a stable/inside partition of the ladder cells, and the bridge disclosure.

### E234 -- a book-level parameter is an average until you measure its members (r1260 bm-b)

E233 measured ONE exponent per panel, but the book holds five instruments with different
liquidity and history (sh588000 only starts in 2020), so the book-level number could be a
mixture charged to four sleeves that do not share it. Estimator B per member gives
sh510300 0.928 [0.830, 1.026], sh510050 0.760 [0.674, 0.847], sh510500 0.416 [0.306, 0.527],
sh512100 0.414 [0.332, 0.496], sh588000 1.456 [1.310, 1.602]: eight of ten member pairs have
DISJOINT intervals, and a pooled fit with five member intercepts lands at 0.622 [0.567, 0.676]
with four of five members outside it. The single exponent is a summary of a spread, not a
property of the book.

The load-bearing part is the cost of acting on that: re-pricing the movement bill with each
sleeve on its own exponent (cost_book(dw) = sum_i c*(|dw|/N)**gamma_i, which collapses to the
linear bill only when every gamma_i = 1) multiplies the bill 1.6x..3.5x -- but almost all of
that is the SPLIT, not the mixture. Charging the same five-sleeve formula with one pooled
exponent already accounts for +1289/+2193/+4015 bp (binary_low/tilt_step/tilt_linear) while the
per-member exponents add only -305/-319/+289 bp. Granularity is a first-order design choice;
the mixture is a second-order correction that can take either sign.

The family verdicts survive both: the toll clears its bar (3.26 over the 15 cells) on 3 of 3
arms under the per-member charge with |t| -6.37/-9.97/-10.27, selection stays inside it
(binary_low +1.32, the tilt arms -0.34), and only 2 of 6 ladder cells change verdict (both the
0.10 band, which is E230's own focus band). The era question closes honestly too: the 2017+
exponent 0.883 sits INSIDE the full-sample interval 0.928 [0.830, 1.026], and re-deriving the
ladder at the era-measured exponent changes 0 of 6 cells -- so no part of that conclusion was
an artefact of borrowing a longer sample's number.

Pit: a pooled fit that drops the lagged magnitude/volume controls is the naive estimator
wearing the controlled one's name, and it reported 0.051 with "5 of 5 members outside the
pooled interval" -- comparing a naive pooled slope against controlled member slopes. Caught
before the face was published, pinned by a selftest leg that asserts the pooled specification
carries the same regressors as the member fits. Sibling: the per-member bill alone would have
been read as the mixture effect, so the same-granularity control is mandatory, not decorative.

Pieces: scripts/e234_per_member_gamma.py (run / selftest, 14 hermetic legs); face
results/state_tilt/PER-MEMBER-GAMMA-<cutoff>.json + per_member_gamma_latest.json; S6 leg
per_member_gamma after empirical_gamma; smoke leg requires per-member intervals containing
their points, a pooled fit carrying the member specification, a compatibility verdict that
names its breakers, and a bill whose mixture term closes against the granularity control.

### E235 -- when two regressors can trade places, the split is unmeasured (r1261 bm-b)

E234 priced the five-sleeve split without asking whose turnover the market prices. Fitting
each sleeve's `log|r|` jointly on its own turnover share and the book's aggregate turnover
(HAC 20, volatility-clustering control) gives two of five sleeves a NEGATIVE own elasticity
(sh510500 -0.122, sh512100 -0.147) and signs that move in lock-step across sleeves, while the
pooled book-scaling elasticity collapses to 0.068 against the family's single-regressor 0.622.
That 5.5x attenuation is channel cancellation, not measured concavity.

Three reusable pieces:
1. **Write the regression in identified coordinates.** With `share = lo - la`, (share, la)
   spans the same space as (lo, la) but is numerically well conditioned; the coefficient on
   share IS the own-channel elasticity and the coefficient on la IS the book-scaling
   elasticity, so `b_agg = beta_la - beta_share` and its error bar comes from the coefficient
   COVARIANCE, not the sum of two standard errors. Pin that covariance against the family's
   own estimator in a selftest leg (here: equal to `e233.ols_hac`'s published se to 1e-9).
2. **A negative elasticity on its own channel is a specification verdict, not a number.**
   No impact story prices a move smaller when turnover is larger. When it appears, the
   published verdict is `unresolved_spec_inadequate` and no figure from the face becomes a
   bill -- the pooled slope would otherwise have cleared the bar and been reported as a
   finding.
3. **A control block that cannot invert is a measurement, not a nuisance.** Aggregate
   turnover is 0.936..0.968 autocorrelated on these panels, so `la` and `la_lag` are one
   regressor: the E233 lagged block inverts on 2 of 5 sleeves and those two flip the sign of
   every channel against the identified block. Publish `spec_stable` per sleeve and demand
   sign agreement before any verdict, rather than reading the block that happened to invert.

Selftest gotchas worth keeping: a single hermetic draw carries ~2.7 sigma of sampling error
at n=4000 with R2~0.1, so recovery legs must average across seeds (a per-draw tolerance is
either vacuous or fails a clean estimator); and pooled member dummies must be indexed by
position among the members that ENTERED the design -- indexing by basket position makes the
first surviving member a column of ones and the design exactly singular.

Runner `scripts/e235_charge_granularity.py` (run / selftest, 18 hermetic legs); face
`results/state_tilt/GRANULARITY-<cutoff>.json` + `granularity_latest.json`; S6 leg
`charge_granularity` after `per_member_gamma`; smoke leg requires intervals containing their
points, `g_scaling == b_own + b_agg` per sleeve, and a negative own elasticity carried into
the published verdict. Follow-up card E236 (share-and-difference design) seeded in the pool.

### E236 -- sign agreement is not size agreement (r1262 bm-b)

E235 left the granularity question open on levels. This face re-asks it with three stationary
designs on the same five sleeves and the answer changes shape rather than settling:

- **differences** `dy on d(share), d(book)` -> b_own 0.431 [0.341, 0.520] t 9.43, b_agg 0.879
  [0.769, 0.990] t 15.57
- **frozen_z** (demeaned share + aggregate level in frozen-first-half sd units) -> b_own 0.017
  [-0.004, 0.038] t 1.59, b_agg 0.101 [0.065, 0.138] t 5.43
- **two_way_fe** (member intercepts + date FE) -> b_own 0.023 [0.012, 0.035] t 3.93, b_agg
  absorbed (the aggregate turnover takes one value per date, so date FE eat it entirely)

Every design agrees b_own is POSITIVE and every one has non-overlapping intervals with the
difference design: span 0.017..0.431, ratio 25.4. Verdict `unresolved_magnitude_disagreement`
-- so the family's single exponent stays a price without a bill and E234's per-sleeve sum is
not a substitute. The negative own elasticity E235 saw does NOT survive (negative_survives
false), and per member 2 of 5 sleeves are sign-fragile.

Four reusable pieces:

1. **Demand size agreement, not just sign agreement.** Two designs returning +0.43 and +0.017
   are not "agreed"; a bill built on the first is 25x the bill built on the second. Frozen
   rule: 95% intervals of any two identifying designs must overlap, and the ratio is
   published beside the verdict. Without this gate the same data names `both_channels_live`.
2. **A design that cannot see a regressor must publish `identifies: false`, never a number.**
   Date fixed effects and a date-common aggregate are collinear by construction; the face
   reports `b_agg: null` with `absorbed.date_fixed_effects = 5233` and the agreement test then
   scores b_agg over 2 readers instead of pretending to 3.
3. **A design with one observation per cell identifies nothing, and must say so.** With a
   single member, within-date demeaning removes the share along with everything else -- the
   fit returns `identifiable: false` ("share carries no within-date variation"). A selftest leg
   pins that a single-member panel never publishes b_own.
4. **Two quantities can wear one name.** The difference design prices a session against that
   session's own turnover change, which co-moves with the same information arrival that sets
   `|r|`; the cross-sectional designs price the share. That asymmetry is the mechanism behind
   the 25x gap and is what makes the surface reading ("both channels live") wrong.

Runner `scripts/e236_share_difference.py` (selftest 18/18), face
`results/state_tilt/SHAREDIFF-<cutoff>.json`, S6 leg `share_difference` after
`charge_granularity`, smoke leg requiring the absorbed-aggregate disclosure and that an
unresolved verdict publishes no granularity charge.


### E237 -- an artefact claim needs a control that is not a component of the dependent variable (r1263 bm-b)

E236 left a 25x size gap between its designs and named the mechanism in prose. This face
measured it instead: the share coefficient (0.431) loses only 0.037 when the market's own |r| is
controlled (0.394), and the first stage says the share never carried market information
(d(share) on d(log|r_book|) = -0.0024, t -1.23, R^2 0.0001) -> verdict `own_channel_survives`,
4 of 5 sleeves survive, sh510300 is `residual_only_channel`. The card's bill rule still refuses
the per-member charge: the two return components both clear the bar (0.1085 [0.1001, 0.1169] vs
0.0730 [0.0658, 0.0802], 7.4s / 9.7s against a 2.77 t bar over 9 pooled tests) but their
intervals are disjoint, ratio 1.49.

Three reusable pieces:

1. **A control that is a component of y is not a control.** dy = d(common) + d(relative)
   identically, so controlling the relative part leaves only the common part and every other
   coefficient measures its covariance with d(common) -- the first draft would have stamped
   "artefact" on a synthetic panel whose truth was a genuine relative channel. The control has
   to be an outside regressor (the market's own |r|).
2. **Refuting an artefact claim is two measurements**: the coefficient under the control, and
   the first stage that says whether the regressor ever carried the confounder. One alone
   cannot distinguish "the confounder was absorbed" from "the channel died of collinearity"
   (the face ships `unresolved_share_dies_without_comovement` for exactly that state).
3. **Direction belongs to the design, not to the analyst.** d(share) + d(book) = d(own), so the
   turnover-direction version of the artefact test is a 1.0/1.0 split regardless of the data;
   the share designs keep E236's direction (dy on turnover changes) and the components designs
   take the card's (turnover on return components), and no coefficient is compared across them.

Runner `scripts/e237_information_structure.py` (selftest 18/18), face
`results/state_tilt/INFOSTRUCT-<cutoff>.json`, S6 leg `information_structure` after
`share_difference`, smoke leg requiring a live co-movement reading beside the verdict, the
published identity residual, and a refused gate that prices no granularity charge.

### E238 -- a denominator that contains the numerator is not a control, and the fix can go either way (r1264 bm-b)

E236/E237 chased an own-turnover coefficient that came out 25x apart depending on design, and
E237 left "what it measures" unnamed. The cheapest remaining explanation was arithmetic: the
share is own turnover over BOOK turnover, and the book is the same five members, so every
member's own turnover sits inside its own denominator. This face rebuilt the book EXCLUDING the
member (leave-one-out) and re-ran the same three designs on the identical sessions
(13,911 pooled differenced rows, 2026-10-29 cutoff).

The answer splits by design, and that is the point:

- **differences** (design A): inclusive 0.4371 [0.3467, 0.5275] -> leave-one-out
  0.5963 [0.5100, 0.6825], gap -0.1592 with block-bootstrap [-0.1778, -0.1359]. Removing the
  member from its own book makes the coefficient BIGGER, so the inclusive denominator
  ATTENUATES; a denominator artefact would have killed it. Verdict
  `own_channel_survives_the_denominator` (4 of 5 members, sh510300 unresolved).
- **frozen_z** (design B): inclusive -0.0366 [t -3.68] -> leave-one-out +0.0013 [t 0.14]. The
  level design's reading WAS the share arithmetic: gap -0.0379 against a predicted -0.0354
  (93% of the gap), verdict `own_channel_is_a_denominator_artefact`.
- **two_way_fe** (design C): 0.02346 -> 0.02289, invariant to three decimals. The date fixed
  effects absorb the book, so the denominator never entered this design at all.

Reusable pieces:

1. **Publish the mechanical prediction, not just the gap.** With own share w the regression is a
   reparameterisation of one object, so the gap the arithmetic predicts is
   `kappa*(b_own_loo - b_agg_loo)` with `kappa = w/(1-w)`. Realised turnover share on this panel
   is 0.218 (kappa 0.279), NOT the nominal 1/5 (kappa 0.25) - the book is equal-weight in
   capital, not in turnover, and the per-member shares run 0.03..0.46. Only with that number
   beside it can the measured gap (-0.159) be read: arithmetic accounts for 0.049 of it and
   points the same way, so ~0.11 is a real effect and the artefact label is correct only for
   the design where the prediction covers the whole gap.
2. **A constant share makes the inclusive design degenerate.** If the own share never moves, the
   inclusive regressor is constant up to floating-point dust and OLS on dust returns 3.8e13 with
   a confident t. The runner refuses below `SHARE_SD_FLOOR=1e-8` and the selftest pins both the
   refusal and the leave-one-out design staying estimable - "the coefficient exists only because
   the share moves" is the sharpest form of the mechanical argument.
3. **The regressor identity is exact, so pin it as an assertion.** d(share)_incl -
   d(share)_loo = d(log rest) - d(log agg) = -d(log(1-w)) to 0.0e+00 on every member. The two
   denominators are two restrictions of one regression, so their disagreement is never evidence
   about the market by itself.
4. **Bootstrap the paired gap, but only the point estimate.** 400 block replicates (20-session
   blocks, dates resampled jointly so the pooled cross-section stays aligned) of a lean normal-
   equation fit ran in 29s; re-running the Newey-West covariance inside each replicate would buy
   nothing and cost minutes.

Runner `scripts/e238_leave_one_out_book.py` (selftest 8/8), face
`results/state_tilt/LOOBOOK-<cutoff>.json` + `loo_by_member_<cutoff>.csv`, S6 leg
`leave_one_out_book` after `information_structure`, smoke leg requiring both denominators with
intervals, the identity as a number, and the artefact label only where the predicted gap sits
inside the measured gap interval. No charge, no adoption: E239 asks the next question the
leave-one-out book raised (in the rest-free book the cross coefficient 0.771 exceeds the own
0.596, which is either economics or the units of summing four members).

### E239 -- a sum of four members is not four counterparties: price the channel per pair (r1265 bm-b)

E238 left an ordering it could not price: in the leave-one-out book the REST coefficient
(0.771) exceeded the own coefficient (0.596). Two readings survive -- an economic statement
(a member's own turnover matters less than the rest of the book's) or a unit (the rest
aggregate is the SUM of four members, so one log point of it is four participants' worth).
Rescaling the sum to a mean cannot settle it: it multiplies the coefficient by four and leaves
every t-statistic and every interval width unchanged. The only apples-to-apples form is per
pair -- regress dy on d(log own) and on d(log other_j) for each other member separately, same
HAC lag, same fixed effects, same break bar, then compare own against the MEAN single-member
cross (13,911 pooled pair rows, 20 ordered pairs, cutoff 2026-10-29).

The answer, and it is not the one E238's ordering suggested:

- **pair fixed effects**: own 0.797 [0.748, 0.846] vs cross 0.314 [0.274, 0.353],
  difference 0.484 [0.408, 0.560] against a multiplicity bar of |t| >= 3.227 (two-sided 5%
  over 20 pairs).
- **member + date fixed effects** (denominator-invariant per E238): own 0.539, cross 0.055,
  difference 0.484 with interval [0.438, 0.530]. The difference point estimate is identical to
  three decimals across the two designs, so the ordering is not an artefact of which fixed
  effects are absorbed.
- **the sum's own coefficient is only 54% of what four counterparties imply**: mean
  single-member cross 0.356 (20 pairs, range -0.242..1.128, 15/20 positive), so 4 x 0.356 =
  1.425 against E238's published rest 0.771 -> ratio 0.541. The aggregate is not an additive
  sum of participant impact; roughly half of what a single counterparty carries does not
  survive in the sum.

Reusable pieces:

1. **"Rescale the aggregate" is not a control.** Dividing a regressor by a constant changes a
   coefficient by that constant and leaves the t-statistic, the interval width and the sign of
   the difference untouched. When the units are the objection, the fix is a different
   REGRESSOR (one counterparty, not the sum), not a different scaling.
2. **Pair fixed effects belong in the demeaned coordinates, not in 20 dummies.** Within-block
   demeaning of y, d(log own) and d(log other) is exactly the pair intercept and keeps the
   design matrix at k=3, so the HAC sandwich stays tractable (20 pairs x ~1400 rows, lag 20).
   Same estimator, different coordinates.
3. **Publish the mean of the published members.** The mean cross must be machine-derived from
   the per-pair list and the smoke leg asserts `|mean(list) - published_mean| < 1e-9`; a summary
   that prints a mean no reader can recompute is a second estimator nobody audited.
4. **Prove the machinery ran before believing any equality** (E188/r1261 family): assert pairs
   fitted == pairs total == 20, pooled rows > 5000 and both regressor sds above the dust floor
   inside the selftest, not only in the runner.
5. **A dust counterparty regressor is refused per pair, not fitted.** A member whose turnover
   never moves has no cross variation; that pair is reported with a reason, and if every block
   is dust the pooled design returns `unresolved_no_pairs` rather than a number.
6. **Read the previous face, never restate its numbers.** The 4x cross-versus-rest comparison
   machine-reads `loobook_latest.json` and declares its own absence (`available: false`) if the
   file is missing -- hand-copied constants in a follow-up face are how a family silently drifts.

Runner `scripts/e239_own_vs_cross.py` (selftest 11/11), face

### E240 -- a published coefficient is only comparable inside its own parametrisation (r1266 bm-b)

E239 published ratio 0.541 by dividing E238's rest coefficient (0.771) by four times the mean
single-counterparty cross slope (1.425). Both halves of that division are read in the wrong
coordinates, and the two errors do not cancel.

1. **0.771 is the book-scaling coefficient, not the rest coefficient.** E238's design is
   `dy on d(share_m), d(log agg)`; its published `loo_b_agg` is the coefficient on d(log agg).
   Writing the same regression in per-counterparty coordinates, `B = a + c` and
   `A = a - kappa*c` with `kappa = w/(1-w)`, so `c = (B - A)/(1 + kappa)`: the rest channel
   behind the published pair (0.596, 0.771) is 0.140 at the nominal w = 1/5, not 0.771.
   Reading `loo_b_agg` as "the rest channel" quotes the whole book against a quarter of one
   counterparty.
2. **Four times one counterparty is not the sum.** The right comparator is one counterparty,
   because the additive world makes the sum-of-four slope EQUAL to the per-counterparty slope:
   `y = c*S` partialled on own leaves the sum slope at exactly c, whatever rho is. So the
   reading is not "keeps 54%" but "keeps 0.138 against one counterparty's 0.183".
3. **The naive pair slope is inflated by omission, and the inflation is measurable.** A pair
   regression with own and ONE counterparty stands in for k counterparties, so its slope is
   `c*(1+(k-1)rho - k rho^2)/(1-rho^2)`: on this book rho = 0.424 and the factor is 1.89. Any
   comparison that starts from the raw pair slope inherits that factor.
4. **The identified test needs no algebra at all.** Regress on own, one counterparty, and the
   sum of the other three -- one and the sum-of-three are in the same units, no channel is
   omitted, and additivity predicts equal coefficients. Measured: one 0.183, three 0.175,
   difference +0.008 [-0.012, +0.022] -> the rest channel adds up.
5. **Two controls that cannot be built are published as refusals, not skipped.** The
   leave-one-out book move is exactly SUM/(k-1) (measured max deviation 0.0), so (own, sum,
   book) is singular; and the two-way FE form of the same design puts the total book move into
   the date effect, which makes the within-transformed sum regressor minus own (residual
   correlation -1.0). A face that quietly dropped these would look cleaner and say less.
6. **A published pair that does not reproduce is a finding.** Re-running E238's coordinates on
   this face's grid gives (A, B) = (-0.333, -0.174) against the published (0.596, 0.771). The
   gap is published with the face (`parametrisation_check.gap_A/gap_B`) instead of being
   reconciled by assertion; the rotation is next round's work, not a footnote.
