### E289 - a unit word in a count's name is a checkable claim only inside its own scope (r1311 bm-b)

A count field's name (`n_rows`, `n_seeds`, `cells_compared`) reads like a claim a reader can audit,
but it is auditable only when the records the name points at are published in the SAME scope as the
count. Measure the two halves separately or the honest answer ("nobody can check this") gets reported
as a clean bill. Case measured (32 dated BAND faces): 894 unit-named integer fields, of which 27
(3.0 pct) sit next to a sibling list keyed exactly the claimed unit -- and all 27 count what their
name says (0 slips). The other 867 split into 301 where the face publishes that unit somewhere else
(the NAME lacks a scope: BANDTRANSFER publishes `flat.cross:200.n_rows = 2` beside a single unrelated
16-row `rows` list, so a face-wide lookup would publish a slip that does not exist) and 566 where the
face publishes no records of that unit at all (the count is a design parameter such as a draw budget).
The two halves need different fixes -- a name change versus a missing record face -- so summing them
into one "unchecked" number tells a reader to fix the wrong thing.

Three rules that make the census trustworthy: (1) the claimed unit is read STRICTLY (`n_rows`,
`num_rows`, `rows_count`, bare `rows`); subset names (`rows_where_tails_disagree`,
`arms_mismatched`) are disclosed as qualified and never judged -- judging them by their unit word is
the E208 false positive (a real quote rejected by a naive word match), and there are 557 of them here,
more than half the field count; (2) re-derivation needs a SIBLING list, never a face-wide search, and
booleans are filtered before classification (Python `bool` is an `int`); (3) publish the checkable
SHARE, because "every checkable count agrees" and "the name is a checkable claim" are different
statements and only the first one is true at 3 pct.

Evidence: `scripts/e286_count_field_scope.py` (selftest 24/24, run/verify green),
`results/state_tilt/BANDCOUNTSCOPE-2026-10-29.json`, S6 leg `count_field_scope` (verify, <1s),
smoke leg `product: a unit-named count is checkable only inside its own scope`,
digest `research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1311-e289-count-scope.md`.
Pool item `E286-COUNT-FIELD-SCOPE` (pool E286 -> card E289).

### E290 - co-location is not evidence: self-auditable counts need their own records AND no equal-length rival (r1312 bm-b)

E286 could say WHICH counts are checkable (27 of 894) but not whether copying the checkable faces would
help a new author. Answering that needs the shape, and the shape has three parts that are easy to
conflate: the count sits beside a list of exactly the unit its name claims (27/27 do), the count EQUALS
that list's length (27/27 do), and no OTHER list of the same unit in the same face happens to have that
length -- and that last one fails 12 of 27 times. An equal-length rival is published as an ambiguity,
not a clean bill: with `summary.rows` (2 rows) and `tags.labels` (2 labels) in one face both length 2, a
`n_rows = 2` agreement cannot be told from a coincidence of size. Co-location alone proves nothing; the
agreement plus the absence of an equal-length rival is the whole test.

Second measurement, and the one that changes an instruction into a number: the pattern's coverage
INSIDE its own exemplars is 27 of 151 of their unit-named counts = 17.9 pct, against 3.0 pct
family-wide. "Publish like these five faces do" therefore multiplies your odds sixfold and still leaves
five of six counts un-auditable, because those faces publish plenty of counts with no records in scope
too. Report the exemplar's own rate before recommending it.

Third: the un-derivable majority is two work items with unrelated costs. 301 rows sit over 299 distinct
scopes -- the face already publishes that unit somewhere, so the fix is to move the count into that
scope or name the scope it counts. 566 rows sit over just 8 keys (draws 253, n_records 115, n_seeds 96,
seeds 56 ...) -- those units are never enumerated anywhere, so no naming convention can rescue them and
they stay un-auditable by design. Never add the halves into one "fixable" number.

Evidence: `scripts/e290_selfauditable_face_profile.py` (selftest 15/15, run/verify 0 problems),
`results/state_tilt/BANDSELFAUDIT-2026-10-29.json` + `bandselfaudit_latest.json`, S6 leg
`self_auditable_face_profile` (verify, 0.29s), smoke leg `product: a count is self-auditable only when
its own records share its scope`, digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1312-e290-self-audit-shape.md`.

### E291 - an equal length is the face's shape repeating: publish a flag's base rate and its mechanism, not just its rate (r1313 bm-b)

E290 flagged 12 of 27 checkable counts as ambiguous because another list of the same unit in the same
face has the same length. That flag only informs if equal lengths can be accidents, and they mostly
cannot be. The RATE is the base rate: 12 of 27 against 10.78 expected from the pooled length mix
(39.9 pct, tail p=0.384), and all 12 rows come from just TWO (face, unit) scopes -- `BANDFLIPBUDGET ::
cells` (8) and `BANDGAPCEILING :: rows` (4) -- so twelve labels are two observations. The MECHANISM is
not chance at all: of 746 equal-length pairs, 605 share a record schema with different rows (81.1
pct), 135 are the very same content (18.1 pct, i.e. 135 duplicated lists nothing else reports) and only
6 differ (0.8 pct). At list level the concentration is ABOVE the null (104 of 125 = 83.2 pct against
67.4 pct expected, p<0.001) because a face draws its arms from one schema; the pooled mix is lopsided
to begin with (24 appears 50 times, 4 thirty-five times). So "two same-unit lists of the same length"
marks shared shape -- and catches duplicates -- rather than two lists competing for one meaning.

Three laws. (1) A rate is only readable beside its null and its tail: 12-vs-10.78 has no story without
the 39.9 pct, and the verdict rule therefore requires BOTH a tail beyond alpha AND a structural share
below 0.5 before it may call an ambiguity real -- a high base rate must not be able to manufacture a
conflict. (2) Publish the independent unit count, not only the row count: eight rows from one scope
inflate the evidence sixfold. (3) Classify the equal-length pair by content before calling it a
near-miss: alias / same-schema / different-content is a partition, and an alias is a duplicate, never
an ambiguity. Sibling pit, fourth sighting: `e286.face_universe()` excludes only E286's own faces, so
E290's `BANDSELFAUDIT-*` face sits inside the census (33 faces, not 32) -- a successor must filter its
sibling's face by name and assert both absences. Evidence: `scripts/e291_ambiguity_chance.py` (selftest
17/17, run/verify 0 problems), `results/state_tilt/BANDAMBIENT-2026-10-29.json`, S6 leg
`ambiguity_by_length_chance`, digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1313-e291-ambiguity-by-length-chance.md`.

### E292 - a published face is a vintage: a sibling-censusing study must re-derive against the universe it published (r1314 bm-b)

The BAND family's studies census each other's published faces, so the universe a study reads GROWS by one
face each time a sibling publishes -- and a `build()` that re-reads the live directory silently rewrites
the older face's summary. Four smoke legs (81/82/86/87) went red for this and nothing was wrong with the
numbers: E286 re-derived over 34 faces where it had published 32, E281 34 vs 27, E282 67 vs 55. Three
reusable rules. (1) Freeze re-derivation to the published vintage and prefer the face's OWN stored name
list (`e286.faces_censused`, `e281.source_faces`, `e282.scope_census` names): a timestamp rule cannot
tell "published after this study" from "re-run after this study" -- `BANDPATH-2026-10-30.json` was
already inside E286's 07:35 universe and was rewritten at 07:44, so a stamp cutoff over-drops it and
leaves the summary two fields short. (2) A new run is the ONLY thing that widens the universe
(`build(extend=True)` in `run()`, frozen by default everywhere else) and the drop must be DISCLOSED on
the face (`universe_vintage`: faces_used / faces_in_directory_now / faces_excluded_as_later) -- a silent
freeze would trade one lie for another. (3) A face whose growth is nobody's re-derivation is still not
green: publish the vintage from birth (E293 did) and seed the audit of the remaining unfrozen studies
instead of trusting that no other leg drifts. Evidence: `scripts/e_band_family_vintage.py` (selftest 6/6,
folded into E286's legs), E286 selftest 25/25, E281/E282/E291/E293 `verify` 0 problems,
`results/state_tilt/BANDDUPES-2026-10-29.json`, digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1314-e293-duplicate-lists-and-vintage-freeze.md`.


### E294 - a number called a multiplier is not a ruler: sign the axis before comparing (r1315 bm-b)

E287 had to answer whether the family's published ceiling (2.2963) is the widest multiplier anything
publishes, and six dated faces carry a field called `multiplier` / `multiplier_max`. Signing them
first dissolved most of the question: only two are band-edge multipliers (E258's per-window draw
multiplier, E257's borrowed ladder range); E272's tail ranges are the instrument the ceiling was read
OFF, so using them as supply compares the ceiling with itself; BANDDISAGREE/BANDDEFLATE restate the
same flips, which is a demand and not a supply; and the three numbers that LOOK wider are on other
rulers entirely -- 63.03 pct is a relative tolerance a test could allow, 2.0327 is a threshold in
spreads on the normalised gap. A comparison is legal only between two readings of the same quantity,
so axis, direction (requirement vs supply) and basis (central value vs most extreme single seed) must
be published per reading, and an off-axis number refused WITH its reason -- otherwise a reader cannot
tell a number that was considered from one that was missed.

Two reusable mechanics. (1) Report both offers and declare which one the verdict uses: the
conservative cap (per-window median) reached 1 of 2 gap rows, the single best seed reached both, and
no reading reached any of the 6 rows above the ceiling (nearest 3.8 pct short, while the mirror-image
narrowing instrument missed its nearest row by 3.7 pct). A verdict stated at the conservative reading
with the optimistic one printed beside it is the only form that can be read as neither boast nor
dismissal. (2) A "closest row still short" helper must handle a closed class -- both gap rows being
reached produced a null where the reader expects a number, so the block publishes
`all_rows_reached_at_optimistic` instead of a fabricated nearest. Two selftest legs written first were
wrong in the same way: "every narrowing reading is below 1.0" is false because a widening multiplier's
per-seed MINIMUM can still exceed 1, and the leg now pins the partition that actually holds (every
widening cap >= 1, at least one narrowing cap < 1). Evidence: `scripts/e287_supply_ceiling_axes.py`
(selftest 22/22, verify 0 problems), `results/state_tilt/BANDSUPPLY-2026-10-29.json`, S6 leg
`supply_ceiling_axes`, digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1315-e287-supply-ceiling-axes.md`.


### E295 - a replay control must be pinned to the reference's own window, and a published rounded copy is compared at its own precision (r1316 bm-b)

Two smoke legs were red on faces that were themselves correct, and both reds were the CHECK, not the
science. (1) E243's headline cell is a replay of E240's numbers, but the cell was built on the live
panel: the panel prints one new session every trading day, so the "control" re-derived over 1329
sessions against E240's published 1328 and read `MISMATCH` on a 5.15e-5 / 2.65e-5 gap against a 1e-9
tolerance. Pinning the cell to the reference's OWN window (`book.first/book.last` in the E240 face)
makes both gaps exactly 0.0 -- so the drift was vintage, not reproduction (E292/E294 family). A replay
means same data AND same window; the face now publishes `window_used`, `window_source`,
`live_panel_last` and `sessions_past_the_pinned_window` (1 this round) so the excluded sessions are
disclosed rather than silently dropped, and it refuses a window that does not apply to this panel
(ends after the panel's last session, or keeps fewer than MIN_SESSIONS) with the reason printed.

(2) E233 publishes its gamma point set ROUNDED to 6 dp while the interval beside it is full
precision, and the leg compared the two at 1e-9 -- so a 6-dp copy of the endpoint (0.829856 vs
0.8298563090732277) read as "an endpoint is missing from its own point set". A rounded publication
must be compared at its own resolution, and the precision has to be published by the face
(`gamma_points_decimals`) rather than defaulted by the reader; the tolerance is then one rounding
unit (1e-6), which still separates a genuinely absent endpoint by seven orders of magnitude. The same
face now also publishes `gamma_points_sources`, and the leg requires the first three points to be
NAMED `interval_lo` / `point` / `interval_hi` -- being numerically inside the interval is a weaker
claim than being the endpoint.

Two reusable rules. (a) Any control/replay cell must be pinned to the reference's declared window and
disclose the readings it excluded; an unpinned re-derivation turns a data vintage into a false
reproduction failure, and a false failure is expensive in exactly the direction that matters (the
cheapest "fix" is to relax the tolerance). (b) A comparison tolerance is a claim about the printed
resolution: full-precision tolerances on rounded publications manufacture reds, and the fix belongs in
the publisher (declare precision + provenance), never in a blanket tolerance bump. Evidence:
`scripts/e243_additivity_out_of_sample.py` (selftest 16/16, +2 legs: "replay survives a panel that
grew", "replay says when it had no window"), `scripts/e233_empirical_gamma.py` (selftest 13/13),
`results/state_tilt/addos_latest.json` (`e240_replay.status=reproduced`, gaps 0.0),
`results/state_tilt/empirical_gamma_latest.json`, smoke legs E243/E233 (both extracted verbatim and
executed standalone: PASS), digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1316-e297-two-red-legs.md`.


### E296 a below-floor flip needs the band NARROWED -- measure the mirror polarity before you quote "unreachable"

The band family partitions its twelve flips against a published floor of 1.0 and a published ceiling
of 2.2963. Everything above the ceiling is a WIDENING demand (the band must be scaled up); the two
rows below the floor are the opposite object -- they need the band CONTRACTED, so an instrument
that widens reaches them in the wrong direction. Two consequences are worth carrying as method.

First, the yardstick must be published before the distance is quoted. E285 ships a per-row
`distance_below_tight_lo_pct` column; its implied reference (flip / (1 - pct/100)) is 1.0283 and
1.5815, i.e. both ABOVE the floor, so that column gauges a narrowing demand with a widening
instrument and its two percentages (13.5 / 60.1) are not distances to the thing the rows need.
Against the one sub-1.0 band-edge multiplier the family actually publishes (0.9220216, the
counterfactual 5 pct band) the rows sit 3.67 pct and 46.26 pct short. A percentage is only a
distance once its reference is on the page.

Second, tightening has a price on the other polarity. Scored against all twelve rows on each row's
own polarity, that same instrument reaches 0 -- it is far below every widening demand. So "one
instrument fixes the floor class" is false in the arithmetic, not merely unevidenced: a row needs
a multiplier at or above its flip on one side and at or below it on the other. Publish the two
demand sets and the number of rows any candidate instrument reaches, or a reader who buys the
narrowing band to fix two rows silently gives up twelve.

Evidence: `scripts/e288_below_floor_narrowing.py` (selftest 19/19, `verify` 0 problems),
`results/state_tilt/BANDFLOORMIRROR-2026-10-29.json` (+`bandfloormirror_latest.json`),
`Tools/s6_chain_bmb.py` leg `below_floor_narrowing` (rc=0, 0.14s), smoke leg E288 (extracted
verbatim out of `smoke_test.py` and executed standalone: PASS), digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1317-e288-below-floor-mirror.md`.


### E297 one more rung is two questions -- price granularity and headroom separately, and re-derive the margin in the window that owns the ladder

"The gap is small enough for one more rung" hides two independent measurements. Granularity is what a
single step of the published grid buys (adjacent-rung multiplier, matched seed for seed); headroom is
what the grid reaches at all (largest draw count over the base draw count). They can point in opposite
directions and in this family they did: the draw ladder's 70 adjacent steps have a median gain of
1.0699 with 37 of them clearing a 5.98 pct margin on their own, while its span tops out at 1.9254
central (2.4271 at one rung's own widest seed). The margin was never a resolution problem, so grinding
the grid finer cannot be the fix -- publish both numbers or the cheap-looking answer (more rungs)
passes for the fix.

The second rule is about which numbers may be subtracted. A margin is a demand minus a reference and
both carry a window; the headline widening margin here was 3.799 pct only because the demand
(self|200|0, cell all_five) and the cap (written at early_three|60) came from other windows than the
ladder (era_2025_now). Re-read where the ladder lives, the same-family margin is 5.98 pct. A rung is
not transferable across windows: E258 had already measured per-window multipliers to differ by more
than 15 pct, i.e. a borrowed rung prices a different sleeve's null. Demand rows outside the ladder's
window are published as not_graded with that reason, never counted as a crossing and never as a
shortfall.

Third: a crossing that exists at one seed of three is published as seed-dependent. One rung
(tail|100|1920) reaches 2.4271 at its widest seed while its central reading is 1.1151; the face counts
crossing rungs per basis and, when the central count is zero, publishes the residual factor and
declares the interpolation aborted -- the next rung is a larger draw budget, a billable decision, not
an arithmetic continuation.

Evidence: `scripts/e295_supply_gap_closure.py` (selftest 22/22, `verify` 0 problems),
`results/state_tilt/BANDCLOSURE-2026-10-29.json` (+ `bandclosure_latest.json`),
`Tools/s6_chain_bmb.py` leg `supply_gap_closure` (rc=0, 0.15s), smoke leg E295 (extracted verbatim out
of `smoke_test.py` and executed standalone: PASS; FAILs when a graded margin is repointed to another
window or the ladder span is mutated), digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1319-e295-supply-gap-closure.md`.

### E298 a margin has a denominator with a window -- moving it home flips reach verdicts and can inflate the gap 20x (r1320 bm-b)

"Not gradable because no ladder was published for this window" and "no reference exists" are different
statements, and only the second one licenses the word *unreachable*. Here only one of four cells owned
a per-rung draw ladder, so 9 of 12 published demand rows were filed `not_graded`, while all four cells
had already published a single draw multiplier for themselves (E258) at each row's own base draw count.
Re-pricing the same twelve rows with the same arithmetic but the home denominator gradated 10 of 12 and
moved three reach verdicts: two rows that looked reachable under a cap written at `early_three|60` are
not reachable by their own window's supply, and one row published as `in_gap` actually reaches once its
own multiplier is the denominator. The borrowed cap understated every widening margin, by up to 147 pct
-- the row behind the family's 3.80 pct headline is 77.04 pct short at home, a factor of 20 away.

Three rules:

1. **A margin is a ratio of two numbers from the same window.** If the demand carries a `cell` and the
   reference does not, you are not measuring a gap; you are measuring the distance between two vintages.
   Publish the pair (borrowed-cap margin, home-window margin) so the reader can see the artifact.
2. **Count ladders and references separately.** "Only 1 of 4 windows has a ladder" is a capacity
   statement about grids; "4 of 4 have a multiplier" is a statement about references. Reporting only
   the first makes nine gradable rows look unmeasurable, and the cheaper answer (build more ladders)
   passes for the fix.
3. **A synthetic counterfactual is not a per-window instrument.** The only sub-1.0 multiplier the
   family publishes runs on one frozen seed to demonstrate that the floor *can* be broken. It cannot
   stand in as a window's narrowing denominator, so those rows are published with `needs_face` naming
   the exact face required (a per-window narrowing ladder, BANDDRAW's shape) rather than priced against
   a number that belongs to no window.

Evidence: `scripts/e300_window_local_margin_census.py` (selftest 27/27, `verify` 0 problems),
`results/state_tilt/BANDMARGINWINDOW-2026-10-29.json` (+ `bandmarginwindow_latest.json`),
`Tools/s6_chain_bmb.py` leg `window_local_margin_census`, smoke leg E300 (reads the published face,
re-derives it from the frozen sources, and fails if a graded row's reference is repointed to another
cell or another base draw count), digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1320-e300-window-local-margin.md`.

### E299 a fix plan must be priced by where the move LANDS, not only by whether the numbers agree (r1321 bm-b)

A published count can agree with a list of the same unit name and still be measuring something else.
E290 handed 301 un-derivable counts on as "the face already publishes this unit elsewhere, so move the
count" -- a plan with no new data behind it. Pricing that plan row by row (scope of the count vs scope
of the candidate list, then value vs list length) showed the plan is mostly not executable: 24 of the
301 name the unit AS the key (so no sibling list of that name can ever exist in the same parent), 76
have the unit published in more than one scope (a choice, not a move), and of the 201 single-target
rows **not one lands beside a list in its own scope or in a scope that contains / sits under it**.
All 126 agreements come from unrelated subtrees -- and every single one of those target lists holds at
most one item, so the "agreement" is the arithmetic of a one-element list meeting a count of 1.

Three rules:
1. **Agreement is necessary, not sufficient.** Ask where the candidate list lives before calling a move
   clean. `same / ancestor / descendant` scope is a plausible target; `face_root` or an unrelated
   subtree is a coincidence bucket, and it must be published beside the clean count, never added to it.
2. **Disclose the degeneracy of the target.** A list of length <= 1 agrees with any count that is 1.
   Report the share of agreements whose target is degenerate (here 126 of 126, 100 pct) or the
   headline "138 of 217 move cleanly" reads as a majority finding when it is an artifact.
3. **A bare unit name can never be moved.** If the key IS the unit (`arms` beside no `arms` list), no
   sibling list of that name can exist in the same parent -- the scope needs its own records. Price
   those as a different job, and never as "no new data needed".

Evidence: `scripts/e292_scope_fix_plan.py` (selftest 16/16, `verify` 0 problems),
`results/state_tilt/BANDSCOPEFIX-2026-10-29.json` (+ `bandscopefix_latest.json`),
`Tools/s6_chain_bmb.py` leg `scope_fix_plan`, smoke leg E292 (re-derives the face and fails if a clean
move is repointed into a foreign scope, if a bare key is priced as a move, or if V4 is claimed while a
row still lands in a related scope), digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1321-e292-scope-fix-plan.md`.


### E301 a freeze answers reproducibility, not whether the verdict depended on the universe (r1322 bm-b)

r1314 froze the BAND family's census to its publish-time vintage because four smoke legs went red on a
directory that had grown (E286 32 -> 34 faces, E281 27 -> 34, E282 55 -> 67). The freeze stopped the
drift but left the question underneath it unanswered: **was any published conclusion a function of the
directory it happened to see?** Priced by re-deriving every directory-censusing study twice in the same
process -- once against the vintage it published, once against the live directory -- the answer is no:
9 of 12 studies can be varied at all and every one prints the same verdict with up to 34 more faces in
view. The drift was a reproducibility problem, not a conclusion problem, and saying which one it was is
the whole content of the face.

Three rules:
1. **A freeze fixes reproducibility; only a second universe tests dependence.** A face that re-derives
   over a frozen vintage is reproducible by construction -- that says nothing about whether the wider
   universe would have reached a different verdict. Publish both readings side by side and classify
   three ways: stable / flips / does-not-reproduce (the last refuses attribution: the face has already
   drifted for some other reason, so the universe question cannot be answered for it).
2. **A study that owns a freeze switch must be driven THROUGH it.** Passing a staged directory to a
   study whose `build(outdir, extend)` honours `extend=False` runs the same frozen computation twice and
   manufactures a stable verdict -- the tautology this study exists to catch (the first build of this
   face did exactly that for the 4 extend-capable studies). Vary the switch it owns, not the argument
   that looks convenient.
3. **Ask how much of the family the question can even reach.** Only 12 of the family's 54 study
   scripts glob the face directory; the other 42 read named sibling faces, which are pinned by name and
   vintage-stable by construction. Reporting "the family is unaffected" without that split conflates the
   part that cannot move with the part that was measured.

Two operational notes: a census cannot include the census (self-inclusion is refused and asserted), and
each study is measured in its own child process under a wall-clock cap -- the first in-process build
wedged on one study and took the whole census with it, which is a measurement result, not an excuse.

Evidence: `scripts/e294_live_universe_drift.py` (selftest 36/36, `verify` 0 problems),
`results/state_tilt/BANDFROZEN-2026-10-29.json` (+ `bandfrozen_latest.json`),
`Tools/s6_chain_bmb.py` leg `live_universe_drift`, smoke leg E294 (re-derives the top row through the
real entry point and fails on self-inclusion, an inflated family shape, or a stable row whose two
verdicts differ -- 4/4 mutations caught), digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1322-e294-live-universe-drift.md`.

### E298 a control that cannot name its panel is unmeasurable, not safe and not broken (r1323 bm-b)

r1316 diagnosed one replay control (E243's) as re-deriving over the live panel and reading its own
vintage as a reproduction failure; the repair taught that one block to say `window_used` /
`window_source` / `live_panel_last` / `sessions_past_the_pinned_window`. A fix to a face is not a fix
to a class, so the class was counted: of 26 published control blocks in 23 dated faces, 12 are identity
checks (they re-derive from the face's own records, so no vintage can move them) and 14 are replays.
Seven replays declare their basis; seven publish nothing, so which panel they read is not recoverable
from the face at all.

Three rules:

1. **Grade a control on KIND first, BASIS second.** An identity check is immune to the panel by
   construction and must never be scored on basis -- scoring it would manufacture risk where there is
   none. Only a replay can be moved by a vintage, so only a replay can be at risk.
2. **"Cannot say" is a published category, never a default.** Writing `reproduced: false` for an
   undeclared control convicts it of using the wrong panel; writing `true` acquits it. Both are
   inventions. Publish the row as unmeasurable and name it, so the next round reads a list.
3. **A path is not an identity.** Two vintages of the same study carry the same control path
   (ADDOS 10-29 and 10-30 both publish `/e240_replay`, one undeclared and one live-declared), so any
   census, dictionary or smoke join keyed on the path alone silently collapses them and hands an
   at-risk row its sibling's basis. Key on `(face, path)` and repeat the face inside every derived row.

Operational notes: a census living in the directory it scans must exclude itself (the first run
graded 26 controls, the second 27, and `verify` could never pass until `self_faces_excluded` was
published and asserted); and the repair's landing is only visible as a *transition* -- the same block
moving undeclared -> live_declared between two vintages -- so vintages are compared pairwise by
(study, path) rather than read one face at a time.

Evidence: `scripts/e298_replay_control_census.py` (selftest 21/21, `verify` 0 problems),
`results/state_tilt/REPLAYCENSUS-2026-10-30.json` (+ `replaycensus_latest.json`),
`Tools/s6_chain_bmb.py` leg `replay_control_census`, smoke leg E298, digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1323-e298-replay-control-census.md`.

### E304 a tolerance finer than the field's printed quantum is a question about the field, not about the leg (r1324 bm-b)

r1316 repaired one leg that compared a 6-dp point set against a full-precision interval at 1e-9. One
repair is not a census. Prices the class: 42 of `smoke_test.py`'s 320 legs carry a numeric comparison
against a published face; 29 of their 62 sites compare at a tolerance finer than the field they read is
printed with (21 on the field's own measured decimals, 8 on the face-level bound only), and 37 of the 42
faces they read publish no statement of their printed precision at all.

Three rules:

1. **Measure the quantum of the field the leg names, not of the face.** A face's coarsest printed
   quantum is an upper bound over every field it carries; the leg reads one key. `key_profile()` walks
   the published leaves under that key name and takes the coarsest decimals among them, and only when
   the key cannot be located at all does the face-level bound stand in -- labelled `face_level` so the
   weaker rows are separable from the measured ones. Keys that hold only integers or labels are dropped
   before any tolerance is compared: an exact equality on a count cannot be undone by rounding.
2. **A near pair is not a copy.** Pairing any two close leaves "found" `current_dd` vs `cumulative_ret`
   at a 4e-8 gap -- two different quantities that happen to sit close. A copy is the same leaf key
   published twice under different parents, so that is the only pair reported. On the real directory it
   comes back **zero**, and the zero is the finding: the one copy the family had was the one r1316
   repaired.
3. **The same key name in two faces is not the same quantity.** Five sites name one key across two
   faces; the gaps (1.98 on `band_frac`, 0.22 on `share_taken_by_vol`) are published as distances with
   the disclosure that a gap above the tolerance means "same name, different quantity", never a defect
   count. Without that sentence the face manufactures five convictions out of a naming coincidence.

Also: a comparison that is exact equality but carries no numeric anchor (`schema == 'etf-book-registry/v1'`)
is not a measurement and must not be counted -- the first build counted 356 exact equalities, nearly all
of them strings and counts, and reported 292 at-risk sites that were names.

Evidence: `scripts/e299_rounded_vs_tolerance_census.py` (selftest 32/32, `verify` 0 problems),
`results/state_tilt/PRECISIONCENSUS-2026-10-30.json` (+ `precisioncensus_latest.json`),
`Tools/s6_chain_bmb.py` leg `precision_census`, smoke leg E299, digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261031-r1324-e299-precision-census.md`.

### E306 a switch that needs no source edit still has a price, and the price is not the finding (r1325 bm-b)

E294 could not ask three directory-censusing studies whether their verdict depends on the universe,
because their `build()` takes no argument. This study makes them askable without editing a line: the
universe reaches each study through a module-level directory global, so redirecting every module
binding of that global at a staged directory re-derives the study. All three reproduce their published
verdict and none flips (staged 118/120/132 faces against the live 170).

Three rules:

1. **Cost and effect are two numbers, published separately.** A global-redirect switch costs 31 module
   bindings to move (measured, and order-independent -- a leg asserts it); a durable `outdir=` parameter
   would instead thread 6 functions and 10 module-default `load()` calls. A cheap simulation is not a
   fix, and "none of them flips" is the answer to the question -- folding both into one figure lets
   either hide the other.
2. **A staging that is not narrower than the live directory is a tautology.** Publish both file counts
   per row and refuse the "stable" reading when the staged universe is not strictly smaller; a leg
   asserts it. A test that re-runs the same computation twice manufactures stability for free.
3. **A vintage may only be witnessed by a stamp the face publishes.** A freeze helper that falls back to
   the file mtime re-reads a different universe after any rewrite of an undated face (observed: one
   study's staged universe read 163 and then 132 across two runs with nothing published changing). Keep
   an undated face rather than drop it on a guessed date, and pin with a leg that touching the file does
   not move the frozen universe.

Also fixed in passing: `e_band_family_vintage.selftest()` leg V2 was date-dependent (its undated
fixture inherits today's mtime, so it rots once the wall clock passes the frozen fixture cutoff) --
fixture mtimes are now pinned with `os.utime`, so the leg tests the rule and not today's date.

### E308 a published block that names no panel is a question for the writer, not a verdict on the face (r1326 bm-b)

E298 left seven replay controls "unmeasurable" because their face carries no window / pin / vintage
key. Asking the code that wrote them answers five without re-running anything, and splits the
question into three different defects -- plus one that is not a control at all:

1. **The writer's own vocabulary is the first thing to test.** One of the seven (ADDOS) is computed by
   `_replay`, which since r1316 writes `window_used`, `window_source`, `live_panel_last` and
   `sessions_past_the_pinned_window` -- the published vintage simply predates the repair (r1269). A
   stale face reads as an undeclared basis, and the witness is another vintage of the same face
   carrying exactly those keys. Publish the cross-vintage witness with the row: "the writer computes
   it" is an inference, "the 10-30 face carries it" is a measurement.
2. **A basis declared beside the block counts.** Four of the seven declare it one level up -- a
   `basis_note`, `source_faces` + `windows_measured`, `bar_lenient_basis` / `bar_strict_basis` /
   `panels`. A census whose vocabulary only looks inside the block will keep re-reporting these as
   unmeasurable. Scan the enclosing document and keep the witness key in the row.
3. **Two really do derive on the live panel, and their own numbers say so.** REPRO's `reproduction`
   and BANDPATH's `focus_replay_of_e230_global_path` move between vintages with nothing else published
   changing (rows 13,911 -> 13,916; 285.88 -> 289.83 bp/yr). When a block has two dated vintages, the
   drift of its own numbers is the observable consequence of an unpinned basis -- a single vintage
   cannot show it and must not be read as "pinned".
4. **A key whose *name* says "reproduced" is not a reproduction.** Re-running E298 after two new faces
   landed turned its seven rows into nine: the two new ones are `per_leg` counter rows
   (`{rows, at_risk, copies}`) whose leg labels merely contain the word. Ask what the row *is*
   (`/per_leg/` container, or keys that are only counts) before asking which panel it read.

Keeping the keys honest: a writer extends its block after building it (`out["window_source"] = ...`),
so a literal-dict scan misses exactly the field being looked for -- the selftest asserts the subscript
form. And the class a row gets must be catchable by the face's own `verify()`: `recoverable_without_rerun`
is recomputed from the class rather than trusted, and a mutated class is asserted to be rejected.
Also: a census that counts the directory must be regenerated when the directory grows -- three
sibling smoke legs (E298/E299/E302) went red the moment new faces landed, all with the same verdict
"the summary does not re-derive".

### E309 a face-level bound is an upper bound on resolution, not a measurement of the field (r1327 bm-b)

A census that cannot find the key a leg reads has three cheap fallbacks and one honest answer. E299
gave 8 of its 29 at-risk rows the face's coarsest printed quantum when no leaf under the key was
found; pricing those 8 (E305) withdrew every one of them, and the reasons fall into four kinds that
are worth recognising before the next census falls back:

1. **A container is not a printed number.** Three of the eight read keys whose value is a
   `list[0]/list[2]`, a `dict[8]`, or `dict[17]/list[2]`. A leaf walker skips dict/list values on
   purpose (that is correct for measuring a quantum) but the same walker cannot then answer "is the
   key there". Keep a second scan that records container values, or "no printed number" and "no key"
   become the same answer.
2. **"Absent from the face being priced" usually means "present in a sibling face the leg names".**
   Three rows read a key that lives in another face the SAME leg reads, printed at 15 dp -- finer
   than the tolerance, so not at risk. The join that matters is per-leg, not per-face; two of those
   sibling readings were already in the census's own `key_profiles`, one field away from the at-risk
   row saying the field could not be found.
3. **A producer's record list can be empty on the vintage that was read.** `session_open` is written
   inside `per_trader/<id>/detail[]`; on 2026-10-30 all six traders were `zero_pending`, so the same
   key that is a float on a filled day is simply absent. Answer absence from the producer's text, and
   say it is absent *today* -- an empty list is not a missing field.
4. **A boolean flag is a label.** One row read `verdict_at_max_p05` / `verdict_at_min_p05`, which are
   `True`/`False`. No quantum can put a boolean at risk.

How to apply: when a fallback fires, publish the fallback's own count beside the headline (E299 did
publish `n_at_risk_on_face_level_bound_only`; the "29 at risk" sentence is what read as 29
measurements), and price the fallback rows in a second study rather than in the same face. The
withdrawal is the product: a bound reported as a measurement is the defect, and naming which of the
four kinds it was is the whole repair.

### E310 a census that lives in the directory it scans must count itself by STUDY, and a cost read off sys.modules belongs to the interpreter, not the study (r1327 bm-b)

Two sibling smoke legs went red for good the day their studies ran on a new date, and neither was a
numbers problem:

1. **A dated vintage per run makes the self-count drift one a day.** E298 counted its own files
   (`REPLAYCENSUS-*` plus the mirror) into `self_faces_excluded`. Each day it runs it leaves one more
   dated vintage on disk, so the next day reads 2 -> 3 and the published face can never be re-derived
   -- the leg asserting `summary` equality is red forever, and re-running only moves the target.
   Counting the self face ONCE (however many of its vintages sit beside it) plus the mirror once fixes
   it; the raw file count is disclosed separately as `self_face_files_on_disk`, so nothing is hidden.
   Keep a leg with two vintages of the study in one directory -- the single-vintage fixture passes
   either way.

2. **A measurement that walks `sys.modules` is a property of the process.** E302 priced the cost of a
   directory switch by counting imported modules holding the directory string: 31 in a fresh process,
   33 inside the smoke run that had already imported half the tree. The study's own published face was
   therefore un-reproducible from any session that had loaded more than it did. Price the switch
   against the study's STATIC import closure (parse `import` / `from ... import` off `scripts/*.py`),
   so the number depends on the study and not on the interpreter (28 either way). Leg it by
   registering an unrelated fake module that binds the same directory and asserting it is never
   counted.

3. **A fallback that keeps the honest default still has to be disclosed.** The vintage helper's mtime
   fallback is right (an undated face cannot be shown to postdate the study, so it is kept, never
   dropped on a guess) and yet silent: touch the file and the same face leaves the universe. E307
   measured all ten consumers and found today's exposure is zero -- the one undated face among 176 is
   not in any stamp-vs-cutoff universe, and the consumer that does stage it reads `generated` itself
   (E302 refuses the fallback on purpose). The repair is therefore disclosure, not a rule change:
   `vintage.undated(outdir, names)` names the mtime-witnessed set so a consumer can publish it.

How to apply: before publishing any census of a directory you also write into, ask two questions --
"can this count change because I ran again?" (self-faces, mirrors, own outputs) and "does this count
change because something else was imported or loaded first?" (module scans, caches, env). Both answers
must show up in the face as disclosures if they genuinely co-move, or be excluded from the measurement
if they do not. A red leg that survives re-running the study is telling you the rule moved, not the
data.

### E311 a tolerance gate is scoped to a question, not to a face -- pair a leg to a gate only through the producer's own comparison (r1330 bm-b)

Pricing "is this leg tighter than the face's own tolerance?" by face produces 18 bands; asking the
writers produces 1. Three readings stand behind the difference:

1. **A published tolerance is usually a parameter of the producer, not a promise about the face.**
   Six band faces carry `frozen_spec.tolerance = 1e-12`, and the legs reading them compare counts,
   verdicts and percentages -- 0.0-slack exact equalities on integers. Arithmetically each is
   "tighter than the gate"; none can be failed by a difference the gate entitles. Ask what the gate
   governs before asking who is tighter.
2. **Read the writer, not the face, to learn whether a gate is a gate.** Of 11 faces that publish a
   tolerance, exactly one writer is *seen comparing with it* (a source line carrying the key and a
   comparison operator); 28 pairs sit on gates that are declared and never compared anywhere in the
   scripts naming that face. Publish the evidence line with the row so the reading is re-checkable,
   and keep "declared_but_never_compared" as its own category rather than folding it into "tighter".
3. **The gate / not-a-gate partition is unstable under renaming.** On one face, `gamma_tol = 0.1` is
   excluded as a measurement while `tol = 0.1` is accepted as a gate -- the same number under two
   names. Publish same-value twins on the gate row (`same_value_as_excluded_key`) instead of letting
   the name decide silently; the one band that survives scope here is exactly that case.

Two operational traps, both caught in-round: a tolerance-name scan keyed on suffix (`*_tol`,
`*tolerance`) silently drops `required_tolerance_pct`, `edge_tolerance_pct` and `tolerance_fraction`
-- the E208 rule applies to the writer side too, so scan on "contains tol" and publish every
rejection with its reason (35 rows here). And a census that greps producers for a face filename will
find **itself** (docstrings and selftest legs name the face): exclude `__file__` from the producer
set, or the study answers its own question with its own text.

How to apply: any "leg vs gate" or "threshold vs threshold" pairing must carry a scope reading with
it; where the scope cannot be established from the producer's source, the pair is published as a
distance, never as a defect. A band of size zero after scope is a real result, not a failed study.

### E312 a gate is compared with a quantity, not with a face -- resolve the constant behind the declared key, then ask whether the operands name the leg's number (r1331 bm-b)

E311 said "pair a leg to a gate only through the producer's own comparison". Pricing that rule
shows the pairing was still keyed on the wrong name, and that scope is only half the question:

1. **The declared key is a label; the producer compares with the constant it is bound to.** All 30
   band rows publish their gate as a bare constant (`"tolerance": TOL`, `"tolerance": MATCH_TOL`,
   `"rel_tol": REL_TOL`, `"tol": GAMMA_TOL`). A scan for the declared name therefore reports
   "declared_but_never_compared" on 28 of them, while the producer compares with `TOL` and often
   through a parameter defaulted from it (`def verdict_from(..., tol=GAMMA_TOL)`). Resolve the
   publish site to its constant, add parameter-default and rebind aliases, and 29 of 30 pairs turn
   out to have a producer comparison. **Before concluding "the gate is never used", check whether
   you scanned the label instead of the value.**
2. **Scope is not operand identity.** Being compared somewhere does not mean being compared with
   the number the leg reads. In this class 25 rows compare names that never meet, 4 legs name no
   face key at all, and exactly 1 shares the leg's quantity — and the two bands *swap*: the only
   band E311 let stand compares the window edges `lo`/`hi` against `FROZEN_GAMMA ± tol` (a
   feasibility test of the ladder, `FROZEN_GAMMA = 0.5` an assumption), while the open-fill band it
   rejected compares `abs(cost - session_open)/session_open` — the very price the leg reads. A band
   that survives scope and dies on operands (or the reverse) is the normal outcome, not an
   inconsistency.
3. **Publish the form, not just the name.** The surviving row's gate is *relative* while the leg is
   *absolute*: same object, untransportable threshold. Names agreeing is not the same as
   entitlement to a difference.

Four operational traps, all live in this round: (a) raw-text scanning reads **prose** as a
comparison — a docstring carrying "tol" and a ">" yielded `this`, `counts`, `as` as operands, so
comparisons must come from `tokenize` NAME/OP tokens; (b) `1e-06` yields the identifier `e` unless
identifiers are required not to start after a digit or dot; (c) a leg naming no face key is **not**
"disjoint" — give it its own partition or the finding inflates itself; (d) `x in [list]` is an
element test, not a substring test, so a self-inclusion guard written that way can never fail.

How to apply: when grading "is this leg tighter than that gate", walk three steps in this order —
declared key → published value/constant → the operands on both sides of the producer's comparator
(one hop down their definitions) — and publish all three with every row. Where the leg names no
face key, record the question as unanswerable at name level instead of counting it.

### E313 a gate published as one number can change form with the size of the quantity it gates -- a clamped scale (`tol * max(1.0, x)`) is two gates, and a fixed divisor is a normalisation, not a scale (r1332 bm-b)

E312 left one band standing on a name match: the face publishes `rel_tol = 0.002`, the producer
compares `rel = abs(cost - session_open) / session_open > REL_TOL`, and the leg compares an
absolute `abs(_px - r["session_open"]) > 1e-09`. Same names, different unit. Reading all 30 rows
at the producer's own comparison line gives three reusable rules.

1. **The face's unit label is not the unit.** `gate_units` is `unspecified` on 28 of 30 rows, and
   where it is declared it is a label. Publish the form observed in the code, and publish the label
   separately so a contradiction is visible rather than absorbed.
2. **A clamp makes one published tolerance into two regimes.** `abs(v - target) <= tol *
   max(1.0, target)` is relative above 1.0 and a flat `tol` below it, so the tolerance in the
   normalised units is `tol * 1.0` for small quantities and `tol * |v|` for large ones. A consumer
   of the face cannot reproduce either regime from the single published number; either publish the
   floor and the scale, or publish two numbers.
3. **A literal divisor is normalisation, not a scale.** `abs(1.0 - pct / 100.0) > TOL` converts
   percent to fraction by a constant and then applies an absolute tolerance: the gate is
   `TOL * 100` in percent units, fixed. Only a divisor that varies with the data (`session_open`)
   is a scale that has to be estimated, and only then does a breakeven exist.

The deliverable is the scale at which two numbers meet, not a count of wrong rows:
`breakeven = leg_absolute / gate_relative` (t35: `session_open = 5e-07`), plus the transformation
in words, plus a plain statement of the classes where **no** multiplicative scale exists -- a count
is invariant under rescaling, and an `==` leg cannot be entitled by any tolerance. Both are
partitions, not failures.

Trap that cost a rewrite: a count marker must be a whole token. The substring `n_` matched
`session_open` and turned a price into a count; the same class of error E208 killed on the reader
side applies to the writer side. `divider()` therefore returns `(kind, value)` -- `name` for a free
scale, `literal` for a fixed normalisation -- and the count test is a token regex, not `in`.

How to apply: before transporting any published tolerance onto another number, walk
(1) form of the quantity the producer compares the gate against, (2) any clamp inside that
expression, (3) any divisor -- free or fixed -- and only then (4) the arithmetic that converts one
side to the other. Publish the conversion and the breakeven; a shared name is evidence of nothing
on its own.

### E315 a clamp that never engages still costs the reader the tolerance -- publish the switch point and both regimes, and put each number in the quantity's own units (r1333 bm-b)

E313 published that 3 of 30 gates are `tol * max(1.0, x)` and one divides by a fixed `100.0`.
Reading the arithmetic out at both ends gives a rule about what a clamp actually buys and costs.

1. **The two regimes meet exactly, so a clamp is one band with a kink, not two bands.** At the
   switch `x = floor` the absolute tolerance is `tol*floor` on both sides and the relative
   tolerance is `tol` on both sides. Publish the continuity as an identity leg; it is what lets a
   reader trust the two numbers as one band.
2. **What the clamp buys is boundedness as `x -> 0`; what it costs is that the gate's absolute
   size now depends on a scale the face does not print.** `tol * x` degenerates to exact equality
   at `x = 0`. The clamp converts unbounded relative looseness into a flat absolute tolerance.
3. **The decisive number is `0.5 / tol`, not the gate.** A `tol * x` gate cannot separate
   neighbouring values of a quantity below `0.5/tol`. On band-arrival that is `5e11` draws against
   a face whose largest number is `1,920` -- so the clamp never engages and the gate is exact
   equality in disguise. That is a statement about the domain, and it is the one that decides
   whether the tolerance matters at all.
4. **A consumer cannot use a gate the face publishes alone.** 0 of 30 rows are reproducible from
   their own face: `scale` appears in none of them, and no clamp token appears on 26 of 30. Publish
   three booleans per row (`gate_path_resolves`, `scale_identifier_in_a_key_name`,
   `clamp_tokens_on_the_face`) so "not published" is measured rather than asserted.

Three traps, each caught inside the window:

* **A check that raises is a check no mutation can fail.** A removed switch point produced
  `float(None)` -> `TypeError` instead of a red leg; every guard now returns `False`.
* **Mutate the block the consumer reads.** The smoke leg reads `clamped_rows`; a harness that
  edited `rows` made 7 mutations "pass" against a leg that was working. Both views of the face are
  legitimate and the mutation must land in the one under test (7/7 caught once fixed).
* **"The largest number on the face" is a bound, not the gated quantity.** One face maximum is
  `20261130.0` -- a date. Computing tolerance as `tol * x` regardless of the row's regime class
  nearly reported constant gates as "growing"; the tolerance is now computed model-aware and a
  constant gate is asserted not to move with an unrelated large number.

How to apply: whenever a gate is not a single number, publish (switch point in the scale's own
units, tolerance below and above in both units, half-unit crossing `0.5/tol`) and one boolean per
face: can this be reproduced from what the face prints? A tolerance that cannot be reproduced is a
comment, not a gate.

### E316 a zero epsilon is exact equality, and a gate can only be read at a magnitude the face prints -- publish the leg's epsilon beside the gate, or the regime is arithmetic nobody can exercise (r1334 bm-b)

E314 published each clamped gate's two regimes. E315 joined those five gates to the legs that
consume them and found that the join, not the regime, decides the comparison.

1. **`leg_tolerance = 0.0` is exact equality, not a small tolerance.** Four of five
   quantity-dependent legs publish zero: no gate tolerance can ever be as tight, so the leg binds at
   every magnitude and the gate's flat regime is only the loosest place the gate ever gets. Print
   the leg's epsilon beside the gate, and print `null` for the ratio rather than `log10(tol/0)` --
   manufacturing `1e12` there is the same error as printing a tolerance for an exact test.
2. **The crossover `eps / tol` is the number a reader needs.** It is defined only where the gate
   really is `tol * x`, and it says where the two gates swap which one binds. On the open-fill row
   it is `1e-09 / 0.002 = 5e-07` units of `session_open`, below any share price, so the leg binds
   across the live range; at one unit the gate is 6.3 orders of magnitude looser.
3. **A magnitude is only a magnitude of the gated quantity when it is attributable.** Counting every
   numeric leaf put `frozen_spec.tolerance = 1e-12` itself into the bucket and produced "240
   magnitudes inside the flat regime" -- an artefact of the gate's own constant (E207/E208 family,
   third contact). Attribute leaves by the identifier the producer builds the scale on (`prev`,
   `session_open`); when that identifier is not a key on the face, publish a status with zero
   magnitudes rather than a count of unrelated numbers.
4. **A regime nobody can evaluate is a claim, not a gate.** Both faces are unattributable: 5 of 5
   rows do not carry the quantity their gate is rated in, so the two-regime arithmetic E314
   published cannot be exercised by any reader of either face.

Two traps caught inside the window:

* **A mutation leg that cannot change the number is not a test.** Doubling a crossover of `0.0`
  leaves `0.0`; the leg passed against a deliberately broken check until the mutation was moved to a
  row where the value moves.
* **A metric with an identity check at one magnitude and none at another is half-tested.** The
  face-maximum ratio had a `10 ** x * eps == tol` check; the one-unit ratio had none, so a forged
  `99.0` survived. Every published order-of-magnitude needs its own recomputation leg.

How to apply: for every gate, print four things and join them -- the gate, the quantity it is rated
in (with a magnitude the face actually carries), the leg's epsilon, and the crossover between them.
If the quantity is not on the face, say `quantity_not_published_on_the_face` with a zero count, and
treat "the gate is tighter than the leg" as unestablished rather than as proven by a ratio nobody
can reproduce.

### E317 no face carries the reader set for its own gate -- derive the required keys from the regime model, and count same-unit decoys separately from magnitudes (r1335 bm-b)

E315 published what is missing; E316 published what would be enough. Per row, four elements are
required before a reader with no producer access can evaluate a gate, plus a fifth where the gate is
piecewise: the **identifier** of the gated quantity, its **unit**, **one magnitude** of it with the
step it belongs to, the **scale expression**, and the **floor**. Demand them from the regime model,
not from a per-face list: `floor` only for `piecewise_floor`, `scale_expression` only where a scale
exists. Across five rows and two faces: 23 elements required, 3 present, 20 absent, and **0 of 5 rows
lets a reader compute its own gate**.

1. **Two absences, two causes -- do not merge them.** E315 reported `quantity_not_published_on_the_face
   5/5`. Two of those five sit on a face that covers a day on which nothing was compared: every
   outcome counter (`matched`, `dropped`, `breach`) is zero and every per-row detail list is empty, so
   the face has no magnitude to print because the leg had nothing to compare. Reporting that as a
   schema gap over-states the defect by 40 percent. Decide emptiness from published outcome counters
   plus empty list fields, never from a verdict string.
2. **A counter named after the absence is not a rung on the ladder.** `zero_pending_traders = 6` is a
   positive number and it un-made the empty day on the first pass. Exclude counters whose own name
   says *zero / no / missing*; and never declare an empty day on a face that publishes no outcome
   counter at all.
3. **A unit word is not a quantity: count decoys separately and price them.** The schema-gap face
   prints 57 numbers in `prev`'s own unit (`base_draws`, `top_draws`, `frozen_spec.grid`) and not one
   of them is `prev`. Counting them as magnitudes would repeat, reader-side, the error that a name is
   a measurement (E207/E208 family). Instead publish them as **decoys** with the tolerance each would
   produce: the substitution spans 1.5 orders of magnitude (6e-11 to 1.92e-09), which is the price of
   reading a face that looks like it carries the number.
4. **A reader that names its own identifiers will cite itself as the producer.** The first pass
   reported `session_open` as a payload key at this study's own line 87 -- its unit vocabulary.
   Any scan of `scripts/` for a key literal must exclude the scanning file, and should prefer the
   script that *binds* the face name (a writer) over one that merely mentions it, publishing the
   evidence tier so the artefact cannot return silently (E310 family).
5. **An identifier that lives only in the schema is a conditional, not a presence.** On the empty-day
   face `session_open` is a quoted payload key in the producer (`t35_open_fill_verify.py:214`) with
   zero instances published, so the requirement is already met for any day that carries a comparison.
   Publish that as `present_in_the_producer_schema_only`; do not tick the box and do not call it
   absent.

How to apply: when a face is supposed to govern a comparison, publish the four (or five) keys and
test them by **path**, not by value -- an element is present only when a leaf carries it: the
identifier as a whole path token, the magnitude as a positive number under that path, the scale as a
string the producer's own `scale_identifier` resolves to the identifier, the floor as its number
under a floor-named path. Then, separately, count the numbers that merely *look* like it and price
what substituting one would cost.

### E318 a headline built from a name census inherits the census's own defect -- prune counts by token boundary, then split the survivors by whose gate they describe (r1337 bm-b)

E317 counted every leaf whose name says *tolerance* and published "122 published gates are exactly
zero".  One of those names is `n_tolerance_named_not_gate` -- **a count of gates that named a
tolerance without being one**.  A census that prunes a token for being a name-not-a-measurement has
to apply the same rule to the names it keeps.  Re-counted under a count-word guard frozen before any
number was read: 62 of the 1108 leaves are counts, **53 of the 122 zeros are those counts**, the zero
band halves to 69, and the census's other numbers barely move (gate leaves 1108 -> 1046, readable-in-
place share 2.98% -> 3.15%, substitution span max unchanged at 19.5935 decades).  The unpruned
control reproduces E317's five published numbers exactly, so the difference is the guard and not a
re-derivation.

1. **Prune by token, never by substring.** The first cut of the guard matched `n_` anywhere and took
   `law.written_law_tol` = 1e-8 off `results/sina_mf_accept.json`, a real written-law acceptance
   tolerance.  Pruning a real quote is worse than the over-count it fixes (E208), so the guard is
   token-level: a leading `n` token, a `_count` suffix, an `no`/`not` token, or a bare count noun.
   The regression leg pins the exact false positive this guard produced.
2. **A count-word guard must publish what it pruned.** Every pruned row ships with the token that
   pruned it and the value it carried, so a reader can audit the guard rather than trust it.
3. **Ask whose gate the survivor describes.** 68 of the 69 residual zeros sit on faces whose
   top-level `study` is `E<n>_<slug>` -- E299, E305, E308, E312, i.e. this same programme's earlier
   censuses recording somebody else's exact-equality gate.  E317 excluded its own E313-E317 family
   and let the earlier members of the same method through, so the headline looked like a population
   of live gates.  **One** gate survives on a real data face.
4. **A zero tolerance is legitimate exactly where the compared number is a copy, not a
   computation.** The one survivor (`t18_deep_manifest.gates.GA`) publishes its own observed maximum
   beside the zero (`max_abs_close_diff_worst = 0.0`), so its exact-equality test is checkable by the
   reader and passes by construction on a byte-identical re-read.  Nothing else in the surviving
   population can say which kind of zero it is -- that is the real finding, and it is a *reader-set*
   gap, not a tolerance defect.

How to apply: before quoting a census as a population, re-count it under the guard it claims to
apply, publish the unpruned control so the movement is attributable, and classify the survivors by
provenance (a study face is a census, not a measurement).  Face =
`results/state_tilt/ZEROTOLPRUNE-2026-10-31.json`, runner =
`scripts/e318_count_named_gate_leaves.py` (run / verify / selftest 25 legs), chain leg
`zero_tolerance_prune`, smoke leg "the zero-tolerance headline is half counts".

### E319 a census guard that is a list of filenames can never say "is this face itself a census" -- measure the arc, then count how many declarations reach it (r1338 bm-b)

E318 ended on one sentence: 68 of 69 surviving zero-tolerance gates sit on this programme's earlier study faces because E317 excluded only its own E313-E317 window. That is not a bad constant, it is the shape of the mechanism. Swept the whole population under a frozen rule -- a face is a *census* when it carries a **structured row pointer** (a `.json` string whose immediate parent key is a face/path token, or whose container is named for faces) to another study's face; every other mention is prose and is published but never counted.

Of **45 study faces, 31 are censuses** (69%). They make **256 row edges, 120 of them census->census**. **Not one of the 120 is covered by any declared exclusion list.** Ten of the 31 declare something: eight declare **only their own two filenames**, one a glob, and **one** (E317) a hand-typed four-prefix family window -- which still misses seven censuses it counts. **Nineteen** censuses that count other censuses declare nothing at all. One face's rows appear in **14** different censuses; one census transitively ingests **37** studies' rows, 82% of the programme.

1. **"Is this face a census" is a property, not a filename.** Every declared guard in the programme is a list of file names, and the property that matters is what the face *does*. Nineteen censuses do not even attempt a guard; the eight that do guard only themselves. Prefer a derived property over a copied list, and when a list is unavoidable publish the rule that generated it.
2. **Prose is not a row.** The first pass resolved every `.json` mention and produced a different graph from the structured-pointer pass; a mention in a `notes` string is a citation, not a counted row (E207/E208 family, fourth contact). Freeze the pointer rule before reading numbers, publish the prose-only targets separately, and add a mutation leg that folding prose into rows changes the edge count exactly once.
3. **Discovery order is not a version rule.** Picking "the dated build rather than the `*_latest` twin" still leaves two dated builds per study, and the first implementation let `os.walk` order choose: the population moved 270 -> 301 edges between runs on the same disk. Canonical selection must be stated (greatest dated basename), not inherited from the traversal.
4. **Filenames are not versions, so a census's population is not recoverable from its arc.** A row points at a *file*, and that file is rewritten in place: 207 of 256 arcs read "counted face is older", 32 are INDETERMINATE because one stamp carries date granularity only, 16 have no stamp, and **one arc points forward in time** -- a face built at 15:30 whose row resolves to the current content of `E299_rounded_vs_tolerance_census`, which was rebuilt at 22:16 the same day. Granularity-aware comparison is mandatory: plain string comparison of `2026-10-31` against `2026-10-31T04:10:24` manufactures 34 phantom forward edges out of 306.
5. **A census that lives in the directory it scans must exclude itself by study identity** (E310), and the exclusion has to be enforced in the loader, not in an identity-check label. The first run of this study counted its own freshly written face and inflated the population by one study and ~30 edges; the leg that claimed "the study's own face is not in the discovery set" passed because the canonical pick had silently selected the lowercase `*_latest` twin.

How to apply: before treating a census as a population, resolve its arcs, ask what property its guard actually expresses, and price the arcs no guard reaches. Face = `results/state_tilt/SELFINCLUSION-2026-10-31.json`, runner = `scripts/e319_census_self_inclusion_sweep.py` (run / verify / selftest 25 legs), chain leg `census_self_inclusion`, smoke leg "every census in this programme counts other censuses".

## E320 -- an ambiguity span bounds a careless reader, not a careful one

E317 published a substitution span for every gate whose block offers two or more numbers in the same unit; E318 removed the leaves that are counts. Of the **219** survivors, **23 (10.5%) are avoidable** -- the block publishes the gated quantity itself: **16** by the gate's own key pointing at exactly one candidate and **7** by the gate's magnitude printed twice -- while **62 are ambiguous** (two or more identifications) and **134 are unresolved** (nothing names or fingerprints the quantity, so the span is the reading). Removing the identified candidate drops the **median span 1.979 -> 1.347 decades**; the 19.59-decade maximum survives untouched because it is a bare `tol`.

1. **The block label is inside every candidate path.** Matching a gate's stem against full paths makes every sibling match by construction: the first cut reported 159 ambiguous rows, and a block named `recovery_known_answer` matched all five of its own numbers. Match on the path with the block prefix removed.
2. **A unit word is not a quantity name.** `residual_tolerance_bp` stems to `bp`, which names every number in the block. Drop unit words from the stem and publish the row as `gate_key_unit_only`; a stem of nothing is a fact about the face, not a licence to borrow the block's name -- borrowing it manufactured ambiguity for 95 rows.
3. **A census over a mutable directory measures the directory.** The control reproduces all 219 published spans only when the input is pinned to the commit that carries it: read from the live worktree, three rows fail because later rounds rewrote those faces (`GATETOL-2026-10-31.json` shows 1774 added lines, `PRECISIONCENSUS` moved `exact_equality` 22 -> 26). Publish `base_commit` and `read_sources` so the counted population is recoverable.

How to apply: a span quoted as risk must name the channel that would resolve it. Where the quantity is published the span is a careless-reader bound; where it is not, the block is undecidable from itself and no reader discipline rescues it. Face = `results/state_tilt/DECOYRESOLVE-2026-10-31.json`, runner = `scripts/e320_decoy_resolution.py` (run / verify / selftest 14 legs), chain leg `decoy_resolution`, smoke leg "a substitution span is judged by whether the quantity is published".
## E321 -- the name of a tolerance can live on the producing side, and usually does not

A gate whose face never names the gated quantity looks unreadable, but the face is not the only place
a name can live: the writer holds the tolerance in a constant.  Reading the producing script for the
same 196 unresolved/ambiguous gates E320 left standing (single reuse of E312's producers_for /
publish_sites / constant_definition -- no re-implementation) gives three populations: **21 (10.7%)
are named by their producer**, of which **7 sit on a module-level constant** that would survive being
published as-is; **139 write a constant that names nothing** (MATCH_TOL, LEVEL_TOL, GAP); and **31**
have no producer that publishes the key at all.  So the producer side buys about one gate in ten, and
the two dominant cases are a name that was never written and a producer nobody can find -- which are
different defects with different fixes (name the constant vs. publish the producer).

Two readings that produced the number: (1) a dated face is invisible to a needle built from its own
filename, so the producer lookup must fall back to the dated template -- without that step 154 of 196
rows read as 'no producer', i.e. the first answer was a search bug wearing a finding's clothes;
(2) a definition's own comment line is part of what it says about the quantity, so it is read before a
constant is called nameless.  The published face keeps the negative decision per row (no_producer /
no_site), because 'I could not find it' and 'it is not there' are different claims.

### E322 a producer lookup that refuses a face publishes a fact about the search, not about the repository -- separate the reading corpus from the ownership corpus, and keep every date/name shape a writer can use

E321's verdict sentence said "25 gates have no producer that publishes the key at all". Re-asked
with a wider needle those 25 rows are **4 faces and every one of them has a writer on disk**. Three
mechanical steps hide a writer, and each is a distinct defect with a distinct fix:

1. **self-exclusion**: `e312.sources()` drops its own file so a census cannot quote itself; the cost
   is that every face that module writes becomes unowned (22 of the 25 rows are one such face,
   counted once per gate row). Excluding self is right for *reading* and wrong for *ownership* --
   the two uses need two corpora, and the ownership corpus must name which auditors it kept.
2. **date shape**: the template substitution rewrites only `YYYY-MM-DD`; this repo also dates faces
   compactly (`CASHLeg-20261027`), where the ISO pattern never fires and the search silently falls
   back to the exact filename no source spells.
3. **composed name**: `f"p1e_nulls_{cls}.json"` puts the class in a variable, so the published
   filename exists only at runtime; the cure is a name prefix, not a looser match.

Read a refusal as a statement about the needle until a wider needle also finds nothing -- and
publish the step that did reach, because "found" without "found how" cannot be reproduced.
Sibling, both directions of the same trap: the scanner that counts itself as a reader (E204/r1232)
and the scanner that excludes itself and loses its own output (here).

### E323 a wider needle moves a population without naming it -- re-price the headline under the wide rule, then publish what the wide rule would have over-claimed

E322 proved the producer lookup refuses four faces, which makes every share E321 published an
untested lower bound. Re-running the whole 196-row, five-class census under the wider needle gives
a flat answer: **the named count does not move (21 of 196, 10.7 pct)**. All 25 unowned rows relocate
to "a producer is found, but the constant it publishes names nothing" -- the refusal was about the
search (E322) and the *name* was never there (here). A published share that survives its own
needle's widening stops being provisional.

Three things this cost, all of them mechanical:

1. **A needle must keep its directory.** `e322.strip_to_needle` basenames on the way, so the
   "literal" attempt became a bare filename and one face's producer set exploded to 106 scripts
   that all mention `etf_book_voltarget_phase.json`. Seeking a face is a path operation; seeking a
   *name* is not.
2. **Accumulating producers is not the same as widening the needle.** A composed prefix is family
   membership, not ownership: `etf_book_bakeoff.json` composes to `etf_book`, which 106 scripts
   contain, and any of them publishing a key called `tolerance_pp` for its own gate will be
   credited to this one. The first burn moved 7 rows to "named" through exactly that crossing.
   The rule that fixes it: **narrow steps (path, filename, dated template) define the producer set
   when they reach anything; wide steps only serve faces nothing narrow reaches.** Publish the
   naive set beside the attended one -- 28 named vs 21 -- so the false-positive volume of the wide
   rule is a number, not an opinion.
3. **Report a re-pricing in both directions.** 25 rows improved (unowned -> owned, still unnamed)
   and 0 regressed; a census that only reports the direction it hoped for cannot be checked.

### E324 "publishes no key of that name" is usually a composition or a data key -- locate the key before calling it missing

Six gates survived every needle E321/E323 tried and came back as `producer_found_but_publishes_no_such_key`. Read one at a time, **five of the six keys are published in the tree** and the sixth is a face no source can reproduce. The class was never about a missing key.

1. **A card that composes other faces has no single producer.** `PRODUCTION-<date>.json` embeds `"control": doc.get("control")` out of `etf_book_spanning_pre2020.json` and `"controls": doc.get("controls")` out of `etf_book_window_decomp.json`. `tolerance_pp` is published -- as `"tolerance_pp": TOL_PP` -- by the sub-face writer, which never names the card. Any ownership census that asks "does the face's writer publish this key" reports four absences that are one indirection deep. Fix the *map*, not the key: 16 of the 196 census rows sit inside a block their face writer copies from another face.
2. **A key can be a value.** `by_kind[r["kind"]] = by_kind.get(r["kind"], 0) + 1` publishes `epsilon` with no literal `epsilon` key anywhere: the key is the value of a column. "No publish site" is then the correct reading and the wrong question -- the identity that proves it is arithmetic (`epsilon`=39 re-counts to the 39 rows of kind epsilon), not lexical.
3. **A face can be unreproducible.** `PRECISIONCENSUS-2026-10-30.json` publishes `summary.by_verdict.tolerance_silently_defaulted` while **no .py under scripts/Tools/live/monitor/firm contains the string**. The artifact (generated 13:45, committed at r1324 14:24) came from a writer version that was never committed. A face is evidence only if a committed writer reproduces it; before calling a key missing, ask whether the *face* is producible at all.
4. **Two predicates had to be tightened, and both were permissive in the wrong direction.** `writes_the_face` counted `open` as writing, so a module that *reads* a sub-face (`with open(DEC, "r")`) was credited as its writer -- that alone mis-assigned one row to `etf_book_pre2020_wf.py`. And a string on a line carrying `=` is not a key: `kind = "epsilon"` is a value. The fixed predicates (`owns_face`: the name assigned the path is opened in a write mode; `shape_of`: mapping key or item-assignment key only) each carry a fixture leg in both directions.

How to apply: for any "no producer publishes this" verdict, first resolve the row's own path in its face (is the value there at all?), then look for a *sub-face* writer the card reads, then for an accumulation keyed by a data column, and only then for absence -- and when you claim absence, say whether any source so much as mentions the string, because "no site" and "no mention" are different defects.

## E325 -- a face-level orphan is not a naming defect, and "no writer" is a fact about a named rule

E321..E324 measured a *name* problem: for each gate leaf, is there a producer, and does it publish a key of that name. All four took the FACE for granted -- that some source in the tree writes it. E325 asked the layer below over the same 196 rows / 51 faces, and the answer depends entirely on how "can produce" is defined, so it is published as a ladder rather than a number.

Readings (results/state_tilt/ORPHANGATEFACE-2026-10-31.json): the published lookup (E321/E312 producer_candidates, unchanged) reports 25 rows (12.76 pct) on 4 faces writer-less. A rule that demands a writer rather than a mention reports 164 rows / 24 faces. Allowing format templates takes it to 11 rows / 8 faces, and composed paths to 0 / 0. Two separate lessons: (a) the published lookup OVER-credits -- its stem fallback accepts a bare mention, so 139 rows are orphan under writer evidence but "named" under it; (b) the strictest rule orphans the MOST faces, so the ladder is monotone only from its second rung and the first rung must be disclosed as an instrument, not a rung.

What the four writer-less faces actually were, in the order the ladder found them: one auditor's own face (E312 writes GATEOPERANDS; E312's and E321's producers_for drop the calling auditor from its own corpus, so the census could never see its instrument's face), two format-template families ("p1e_nulls_{cls}.json", "REGIME5-DIAG-{cutoff}.json", "PRECISIONCENSUS-%s.json"), and one composed path (`OUT_JSON = ROOT / "results" / "etf_book_voltarget_lag.json"`). Every one of those is a *lookup* artefact, and E322 had already named the same four shapes at key level -- the defect class is at the layer of the search, not of the repository.

Two pits worth carrying. A family credit must not be given to a module that SPELLS the face: if the literal basename is in the source and the source does not write it, the source is a reader, and crediting it through some other family prefix it happens to format turns every reader into a producer (measured: R2 went from 20 to 22 orphan faces and the row count from 157 to 162 the moment the tail test was loosened before the spelling guard was added). And rows are not faces: one face carried 22 of the 25 first-rung rows, so a row-weighted reading says the orphan problem is eight times bigger than a face-weighted one in the same tree.

How to apply: for any "this number has no producer" claim, resolve the face first and publish the naming rule with the count. Enumerate the shapes explicitly -- literal writer, format template, composed path, mention-only, absent from disk -- because "not an orphan" is not the same as "reproduced": the mention-only residue is published separately (0 rows here) or a reader will take "0 orphans" as "every face is reproducible".
