row with no name field) as fixtures. A census whose population keys do not both re-derive
(`published_faces_scanned`, `directory_named_fields`) is refused by the chain.

**Bounds.** Basename-decided collisions count once per row, not per directory; composition is
priced against paths that exist on *this* tree at scan time; a row with several name fields is
`lands` if any of them lands (the published `join_target` says which); faces above 3 MB are
outside the shared scanner.

### E439 -- the directory-onto-a-file-slot class is empty at the call slot: 0 of 40 attributed rows hands a directory (r1458 bm-b)

E438 followed the write inside each callee of the temp-supplying rows and published 56 that land on
a file-path parameter. That count was keyed by callee NAME, and a name-keyed index counts every
`lst.append(x)` as a call to a wrapper named `append`. E439 prices the same class at the call slot
under attribution (the caller must be the defining module or import it) and grades the argument
shape.

**Measured.** 3,454 sources, 310 parameter sites, 11/11 wrappers confirmed live, 27,791
directory-parameter call rows. The name index attributes **24,931** rows to those wrappers;
reachability keeps **40** and drops 24,891 as same-name calls on something else (`write` 16,
`save` 8, `_write_csv` 4, `write_face` 3, `dump`/`run`/`write_json`/`append` 2 each). Of the 40
kept rows **0 hand a directory** (share 0.0): 22 compose a name onto a base, 12 pass a literal
file path, 6 are runtime expressions. E438's 56 re-price to **17 attributed / 39 dropped / 0
handing a directory**. Verdict, recomputed by the gate:
`no_call_row_hands_a_directory_to_a_file_path_wrapper`.

**Why the joint read matters.** The defect is empty for a structural reason, not a lucky sample:
every surviving call row that reaches a file-path wrapper has ALREADY joined a name onto its base,
so the temp marker is a file path by the time the wrapper sees it. E438's temp rows and E439's call
rows are different populations, and publishing 56 -> 17 -> 0 on one face keeps that from reading as
a contradiction. The correction is reachability, not re-grading -- the kept rows keep E438's class.

**Bounds.** Attribution is conservative ("caller is the defining module or imports it"); 33 rows
sit under an ambiguous wrapper name and are kept only when the callee resolves. 6 of the 40 are
runtime expressions whose text resolves to no single expression -- published as `unknown`, never as
directories. A wrapper absent from the live tree refuses the chain instead of leaving a tally. The
write path emits the card's dated face AND a `*_latest` mirror; writing only the mirror had left
`FILESLOT-<cutoff>.json` missing while the card claimed it (fixed in-window, r1458).

### E436 -- the doubling read a double-ready row invites is performed by nobody: 0 of 19 naming read sites join the published directory (r1459 bm-b)

E433 published rows whose directory-named field holds a FILE path while a sibling name field already
equals that basename, so `dir + name` was armed. E436 prices whether a consumer ever performs it.
Population imported from `constdirs_latest.json`: 18 rows carrying a fragment reduce to **11**
distinct `(fragment, resolved_directory)` targets -- row and target counts are different units and
are published side by side. Every `.py` in E423's corpus is parsed and every IO/path call whose
argument subtree spells the fragment literally is graded by the base it composes onto:
`joins_the_published_directory` (the doubling read), `composes_from_the_parent_directory` (rebuilds
the same path from a fresh root), `composes_from_an_unrelated_base`, `base_unresolved`.

**Measured.** 37 sites name a fragment -- 10 read, 9 write, 18 path-only. **0 read sites join the
published directory**: the doubling read does not exist anywhere in the corpus. **8** read sites
recompose the file from the *parent* and rebuild exactly the published path (all of them read
`idle_trigger.bm-c.json`, another machine's health face); 2 more address the same tree through a
`K:\...` literal, so the resolved-path test grades them unrelated; the doubled path exists in 0
cases and all 10 resolved read compositions are absent on this work tree. **10 of the 11 targets
have no read site at all** -- they are written and named, never read.

**Why this is the answer and not a null.** The containment is a property of the read side, not of
the row: a double-ready field is only dangerous if a consumer starts from the published value
instead of from the parent it was built from. Publishing "0 doubling reads" beside "8 parent
recompositions" keeps the zero from reading as "nobody touches these files".

**Two instrument repairs, both caught by the numbers rather than by the code.** (a) The base of a
composing expression must stop *before* the fragment: slicing `chain[1:]` kept the fragment as a
base element, which turned 8 parent recompositions into 8 "doubling reads" composing
`.../results/idle_trigger.bm-c.json/idle_trigger.bm-c.json`. The first headline was manufactured by
an off-by-one. (b) `open` is not a reader: the first build counted `open(p, "w")` as a read, so 9
writes sat in the read tally and every writer looked like a consumer; grading the mode argument
moved them. A family tally is only worth publishing when the family is read from the argument, not
from the callee name.

**Bounds.** A site is attributed only when its composing chain ends in the fragment literal, so a
name built from an f-string, a variable, or a loop is outside this scan and is never counted as
absent. Bases resolve one hop through module constants (string literal, `__file__`/dirname shape,
another name) and stay `base_unresolved` (21 sites) instead of being guessed from spelling.
Existence is tested on the current work tree, so another machine's face reads as absent exactly
like a mis-composed in-tree path.

### E440 -- "dropped by a rule" is not "overstated": 24,308 of 25,015 dropped call rows are method calls, 707 are ambiguous names, 0 are unjustified (r1460 bm-b)

E439 kept 40 of its call rows and published the other 24,911 under one word -- *overstated* -- because
it required the caller file to be the defining module or one of its importers. That word is a claim
about the dropped rows, not a reading of them, and the two reasons a row can fall outside that rule
point in opposite directions: a method call that merely shares the wrapper's name (`f.write(p)`,
`lst.append(x)`) says the name index invented the row, while a bare call to a name several modules
define says the tree has ambiguous helper names. Nothing in E439 could tell them apart.

**Measured on two independent axes, neither inferred from the other.** Axis 1, definitions per name,
imported from E439's own scan: `_judge_lock_acquire` 1, `_syn_file` 3, `_write_csv` 8, `append` 2,
`apply_close` 1, `dump` 11, `run` 300, `save` 18, `write` 26, `write_face` 41, `write_json` 28 --
**9 of 11 names are defined by more than one module**. Axis 2, how the call is spelled at its own
line, re-read from the caller's AST: `attribute_qualified` / `bare_name` / both / not-found. Of
25,015 dropped rows (the corpus grew; E439 published 24,911):

* **24,308 (97.2%) are attribute calls.** The receiver is an object; no module-level wrapper is that
  receiver, so these rows were never evidence about the wrapper at all.
* **707 (2.8%) are bare calls to a name more than one module defines.** Ambiguity, published as its
  own class instead of being folded into the method mass.
* **0 are bare calls to a name with a single definition** -- the residue the rule cannot justify.
* 0 rows had moved off their indexed line (the second axis re-reads live source, so drift is a
  class, not an assumption).

**Three lessons.** (a) A drop is a claim until both axes are read: a reachability rule that is right
in effect can be right for two different reasons, and only one of them says the name index lied. (b)
The name index cannot distinguish `obj.write(p)` from `write(p)` -- that is a property of the index,
so the spelling must be recovered from the caller's AST rather than from the row the index produced
(one parse per file, indexed by `(line, name)`, turns 25k questions into dictionary hits). (c) The
residue needs its own published class even when it is zero: "0 of 25,015" is a finding, while a zero
that exists only as the absence of the other two classes is indistinguishable from a scan that
measured nothing -- so the selftest carries a leg where a residue row *would* flip the verdict.

Face: `results/state_tilt/sharedname_latest.json` (`SHAREDNAME-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`every_dropped_row_is_either_a_method_call_or_a_bare_call_to_a_name_that_more_than_one_module_defines`;
selftest 19/19; smoke leg extracted verbatim 1/1 with a doctored class 1/1 red and the face restored
byte-identical (7abee58ed9b97d4d).

### E443 -- "more than one module defines this name" is a name fact: all 707 of E440's shared-name bare calls bind to the caller's own definition, 0 reach another module (r1461 bm-b)

E440 split 25,015 dropped call rows into 24,308 attribute calls and **707 bare calls to a name
several modules define**, and labelled the second class *ambiguous*. Ambiguity is a claim about
bindings, and a name index cannot make it: `from a import dump` binds exactly one `dump`, and a
module that writes `def run(...)` at top level binds its own.

**Measured by reading each caller's own imports** (one AST parse per file, `from X import name`
including `as`, the caller's own top-level defs, star imports, and `from pkg import submodule`
treated as a module binding when `pkg/submodule.py` exists), over 3,463 corpus sources, with all
11 wrappers re-confirmed live and 25,023 dropped rows recomputed (`distance_check.agrees = true`
against E440's published 707):

* **707 of 707 (100%) resolve to `the_callers_own_definition`.** Not one bare call binds to a
  defining module other than the caller's own file.
* **0** bind to exactly one foreign defining module, **0** bind to two or more, **0** come through
  a module that does not define the name, **0** through a star import, **0** have no visible
  definition.
* The class is a **name shadow**, not a cross-module hazard: 183 caller files each carry their own
  helper. The eight names are the closeout vocabulary -- `run` 323 rows over 65 files (defined by
  **300** different modules), `write_json` 184 (28), `write` 91 (26), `write_face` 48 (41),
  `save` 28 (18), `dump` 21 (11), `_write_csv` 11 (8), `append` 1 (2).
* 622 rows are production callers and 85 are selftests; the row set is 194 cells.
* The surviving definitions do **not** write the parameter path: **0 of 707** compose their
  directory parameter onto a file. The write axis is bounded, not assumed -- 322 of the 707
  definitions could not be resolved from the scan and are published as their own class (317 name
  the directory in a write but compose nothing onto it, 39 do one of each, 29 name it nowhere).

**Three lessons.** (a) A name index can publish *who defines this word*; it cannot publish *which
definition this call reaches* -- that is a per-caller import fact, and reading it collapsed an
"ambiguous" class to a single resolution. (b) The two classes a shared name must be split into are
**self-definition** (the caller's own `def`) and **cross-module binding**; only the second is a
hazard, and here it is empty, so E439's reachability rule was right for a second reason and E440's
ambiguity label overstated a zero. (c) A guard must be priced as well as written: `verify` re-derives
E440's whole scan over 3.4k sources in ~20 minutes, so the S6 leg is `check` -- it re-derives every
published tally from the published cells -- and the full `verify` is published on demand, because a
leg whose only cost is 20 minutes per tick gets switched off (E364's rule, now applied to a second
study).

Face: `results/state_tilt/barecallresolve_latest.json` (`BARECALLRESOLVE-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`every_shared_name_call_resolves_once_the_callers_imports_are_read`; selftest 16/16; verify
problems=[]; check problems=[]; S6 leg `bare_call_resolve` (check, rc 0); smoke leg structural with a
doctored-cell control.

### E441 -- E435's empty composition is 21 live writer directories and 51 frozen ones: 36 of the 385 composable joins sit on a base that gained a member after the face was written (r1461 bm-b)

E435 published directory values that are the home directory of a published face, and **0** composable
joins that lands on anything.  A zero like that supports two opposite readings and E435 could not tell
them apart: either the base is a **live writer directory** (another round writes new members into it,
so a landing target is one round away and the zero is *timing*) or the base is **frozen** (nothing has
been written there since the carrier, so the zero is *structural*).  This study reads the filesystem
rather than the intent: for every face-home row it lists the published `.json` faces living directly
under the named directory, drops the carrier itself, and asks how many members carry an mtime strictly
later than the carrier's.

* **522 rows over 72 distinct directories** -- the population is far more concentrated than the row
  count suggests: `results/state_tilt` alone carries 44 of them.
* **21 directories are live**, 51 frozen; **83 of 522 (15.9%)** carriers were outlived by a member of
  the base they name.
* Of the **385 composable** rows (the ones that DO offer a name to join), **36 sit on a live base**
  and 349 on a frozen one.  The empty composition is therefore mostly structure, but roughly one in
  eleven of the rows a landing target would reach is on a base that is still being written.

**The population is not stable across republications, and that is a finding of its own.**  This face
first measured **626** rows; after the census faces it inherits from were rebuilt in this same window
the number fell to 522.  The 104 rows that disappeared were directory values *republished by stale
census faces* -- i.e. a large part of what E435 counted was other censuses restating the same
directories.  A population whose members are themselves censuses of that population shrinks every
time one of them is refreshed; any count in this family must name the round it was taken in.

**Two exclusions that are different facts.**  The carrier must leave its own member list, or a face
that names its own directory is always its own newest member and every such base reads frozen.  And
this study's own faces must leave the scan, or the largest family reads live *because of the reader*
(E180/E207 self-inclusion, sixth recurrence).  Both are named in `method_limits`; `is_own_output()`
carries four selftest legs.

**Two defects caught by inspection rather than by the code.**  (a) The aggregate directory key was
first spelled `directory`, which put this study's own face back into the population it censuses:
measured in-window at **exactly +144 rows** (72 directories x the dated face and its `latest` twin).
Renaming the key to `base` -- the spelling the rows already used -- removed the self-inflation; this
is the r1234 name-is-semantics law firing on a study about names.  (b) The first distance check
compared 522 style row counts against E435's *whole* directory-valued population instead of the
face-home subset, so it fired on its own correctness every run.

Face: `results/state_tilt/facehome_latest.json` (`FACEHOME-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`some_face_home_bases_are_live_writer_directories_and_the_rest_are_frozen`; selftest 24/24; S6 leg
`face_home_family` (verify); smoke leg extracted verbatim with a doctored frozen directory as the
control.

### E445 -- every one of the 36 live face-home rows composes a doubled path, and the target it is looking for already exists at the repo root (r1462 bm-b)

E441 graded a base live when a member appeared after the carrier and called those rows "one round
away" from a landing target.  E445 composed the row's own name field onto the base, with E435's own
rule, and asked whether the target already exists.

**36 live composable rows over 9 bases: 0 target_already_exists, 0 target_is_the_carrier, 36
target_would_be_new -- and all 36 compose a path that repeats the base**, because the name field of
all three carriers (`SHADOWFACE-2026-11-04.json`, its `-2026-11-05` twin and `shadowface_latest.json`
-- one face republished three ways) is `path`, holding a full relative path such as
`results/tom_overlay/latest.json`.  `join(base, name)` therefore yields
`results/tom_overlay/results/tom_overlay/latest.json`.  **No write into the base can ever produce
that path**, so these rows are not timing at all.

The reading that makes it a defect and not a curiosity: **the same name resolves from the repo root
on 36 of 36 rows** (9 distinct names, all on disk, all older than the carrier).  The target exists
now and only the join misses it.  E441's live/frozen axis was measuring the mtime of a directory
while the reader it stood in for composes a name that is already a path.

Three things this cost, each now mechanical:

* **a composition is a claim about a spelling, not about a base** -- the join is only as good as the
  assumption that the name field is a bare basename; publishing `name_value_is_already_a_path` and
  `composition_repeats_the_base` per candidate makes the assumption checkable instead of implicit;
* **a self-reference is not a landing target** -- `target_is_the_carrier` is its own class, because a
  row whose name field is the carrier's basename composes onto itself and would otherwise count as a
  hit;
* **the same face republished three ways triples the population** -- 36 rows are 12 rows x 3
  spellings, so `distinct_carriers` is what keeps a per-row count from being read as a count of
  distinct readers.

Face: `results/state_tilt/facehometarget_latest.json` (`FACEHOMETARGET-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`no_live_base_holds_the_composed_basename_so_every_live_target_would_be_new` (with
`rows_where_the_target_exists_but_the_join_misses_it` = 36); producer
`scripts/e445_facehome_target.py` (selftest 24/24, verify problems=[]); S6 leg `face_home_target`
(rc=0); smoke leg `e445 face-home target`.


### E446 --- a frozen face-home base is dormant or abandoned (r1463 bm-b)

E441 published 51 face-home bases as `frozen`, which measured one thing only: no member of the
base has an mtime later than the carrier naming it. The word invites a second claim it never made
-- that nothing will ever write there again. Ask it directly: does the corpus hold a write site
whose target resolves into the base?

```text
51 frozen bases -> 28 with a resolving write site (dormant), 23 with none (abandoned)
                -> 7 more reachable only through a literal tail (head unfollowable)
                -> 16 still without a writer once that evidence is allowed
```

Three things it cost, each now mechanical:

* **a read is not a writer, and that is the whole measurement** -- the discrimination lives
  entirely in the mode argument and the sink name (`open(..., "w")`, `mkdir`, `to_parquet`,
  `write_text`, copy/rename destination). 31,152 write-shaped calls over 12,131 walked files is
  the population that survives it; without it every base would have had a writer;
* **a resolver must speak the repository's own idiom** --
  `OUT_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "results",
  "etf_book_production")` is how most constants here are written, and a resolver that cannot read
  it measures its own ignorance: 7 bases left the abandoned set once
  `__file__`/`dirname`/`abspath` and the literal-tail reading were taught;
* **a base that contains another base cannot be abandoned** -- `results` is one of the 51 frozen
  bases and inherits 6,291 sites from the 49 bases inside it, so the population excluding ancestor
  bases is published beside the full one and both verdicts are printed.

The abandoned set splits the way the question wanted: the three rollback/backup directories
(`_r753bmc_churn_backup`, `_r903bmc_ff_backup`, `_r1024bma_rollback_side`) *should* have no
writer, while `results/etf_book_production`, `results/etf_book_order`, `results/m6_regime5`,
`results/t23_census`, `results/e79` and `results/g25` are production directories whose consumer
would read a file no code in this tree can ever create again.

Face: `results/state_tilt/frozenwriter_latest.json` (`FROZENWRITER-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`some_frozen_bases_have_a_write_site_and_some_have_none_so_dormant_and_abandoned_are_different_bases`;
producer `scripts/e446_frozen_writer.py` (selftest 31/31, verify problems=[]); S6 leg
`frozen_writer`; smoke leg `e446 frozen base writer`. Digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1463-e446-frozen-base-writer.md`.

### E442 -- a composition that cannot be followed is not a composition that is dropped: 85 of 16,611 path compositions are provably composed and never used, 2,001 cannot be followed at all (r1464 bm-b)

E436 named 18 sites that compose a path and grade nothing downstream, and left the question open.
This study takes **every** `os.path.join` / `Path / "x"` site in the corpus (3,493 parsed sources,
2,501 files, 16,611 sites) and follows the composed value inside the scope that built it.

READINGS. 13,856 sites reach a consumer from where they are composed (3,153 handed straight to an
opener, 2,415 to another call, 3,995 through a bound name into an open/read/write, 3,415 only
inside a nested def, 530 passed on, 221 returned, 127 into a dict literal). **85 are composed and
never used in their scope, and 2,001 cannot be followed at all** — the value is never bound to a
plain name (f-string, subscript, comparison, an assignment target the reader cannot resolve), so
the method has no name to follow. E436's own residue grades 30 of 30 sites, 3 of them dropped.

THREE RULES MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.

* **An unfollowable site is not a dropped site, and the two must not be summed into one number.**
  `dropped_sites` (2,086 = 12.56%) is the sum of `composed_and_never_used` (85) and
  `composed_where_no_name_can_be_followed` (2,001); only the first is evidence of a dead
  composition, and a headline that printed 12.56% would indict 24x the population the study
  actually proved. Both counts are published separately, and the verdict vocabulary says "some
  composed paths are dropped" rather than pricing the sum.
* **A guard that demands a bound name for every "flows into X" class accuses the cases the card
  names.** The tally required a `binding` for `flows_into_a_return` and `flows_into_a_dict_literal`,
  which is exactly the direct-reach shape (`return join(...)`, `{"p": join(...)}`): 30 legitimate
  rows were reported as "flows out of a name it never bound". The guard now holds only
  `flows_into_an_open_read_or_write` / `another_call` / `a_nested_scope` to a binding (those are
  defined as flows of a bound name), and the direct-reach count is published as
  `sites_reaching_without_a_bound_name` (293) so the shape is visible instead of silently legal.
* **`ast.get_source_segment` splits the whole source on every call.** Asking for one segment per
  composition site re-split each file once per site; the first build was killed at 898 s of CPU
  with no output. A per-file splitter that copies ast's own `_splitlines_no_ff` + byte-slice join
  (lines keep their terminators, columns are byte offsets) cuts the build to **44 s** with a
  8,625-segment / 0-mismatch equivalence check against `ast.get_source_segment` over 80 sampled
  files. Any scan that quotes source text per AST node pays this tax.

Face: `results/state_tilt/deadpath_latest.json` (`DEADPATH-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`some_composed_paths_are_dropped_inside_the_scope_that_composes_them`; producer
`scripts/e442_deadpath.py` (selftest 26/26, verify problems=[], check problems=[]); S6 leg
`dead_path_composition`; smoke leg `e442 which path composition is never consumed`. Digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1464-e442-dead-path.md`.

### E448 -- a dropped composition is almost never a lost write: 25 of the 30 drops that name a path name one that already exists, and 19 of the 85 are superseded by another open in the same file (r1466 bm-b)

E442 published 85 compositions whose value is never used in the scope that built them and graded
none of them. This study grades all 85 by resolving each composition's **parent directory** and
asking whether any opener in the same file lands under it (4,655 opener calls over the 69 files).

READING (85 drops, 69 files): **19 superseded by a wider open** (10 of them an exact re-open of the
same path, 9 only a sibling under the same parent), **30 opened nowhere in their file**, 33 whose
parent is a runtime value (a temp dir, a parameter: `mkdtemp`, `td`, `tmp`), and **3 that are not
path compositions at all** -- `"\n".join(lines)` is a text join and E442's kind detector takes it as
`os_path_join` because the dotted tail is `join`. Of the 30 dropped-where-resolved: **25 name a path
that already exists on disk**, 2 name a path that does not exist (both anchored on the `K:` group
layout, dead code on this host), 2 are glob patterns (`results/trial_labor_w*` defined as
`FAMILY_GLOB` and never globbed), 1 is not checkable.

THREE RULES MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.

* **"Opened nowhere in this file" is not "the artifact is missing".** Six studies compose
  `os.path.join(ROOT, "research", "<STUDY>-P1.md")` as a `PREREG` constant and never open it; all
  six notes exist on disk (hand-authored). The row is a dead *read* pointer, not a lost write, and
  the first version of this face read them as orphans without saying so. The disk probe
  (`on_disk`, read-only `os.path.exists` on the composed key) is what separates the two, and it
  flipped the headline from "30 dropped writes" to "25 of 30 name a path that is already there".
* **The anchor of `__file__` is the whole instrument.** The first version resolved `__file__` to the
  repo root, so `ROOT = dirname(dirname(abspath(__file__)))` landed one level **above** the repo and
  every parent came out as `.../quant/results` instead of `.../quant/bigmoney/results`; the disk
  probe reported 1 present instead of 25. Worse, the fixture was written with the same wrong anchor
  (`dirname(abspath(__file__))` expected to be the root), so the selftest agreed with the bug. The
  fix is to seed the constant environment with the module's own path (`ROOT/<rel>`) and to pin both
  shapes: two dirnames = the repo root, one dirname = `scripts/`.
* **The parent test needs a boundary, not a prefix, and git plumbing is not an artifact.** Parent
  `r` must not cover `results/x.json` (leg 4), and an opener of `rebase-merge/author-script` under
  the repo parent is a git write, not evidence that the file's artifact is produced: those hits are
  published in `ignored_hits` and counted separately, never as supersessions.

Face: `results/state_tilt/droppedpath_latest.json` (`DROPPEDPATH-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`some_dropped_path_compositions_are_opened_nowhere_in_their_file`; producer
`scripts/e448_dropped_path.py` (selftest 19/19, verify problems=[], check problems=[]); S6 leg
`dropped_path_open`; smoke leg `e448 which composed and dropped path is still written`. Digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1466-e448-dropped-path.md`.


### E444 -- E440's 24,618 attribute rows are not "a method on some object": every module they were attributed to defines no class at all, so no row could name a module method (r1467 bm-b)

E440 dropped 24,308 attribute call rows with one sentence: the receiver is an object, not a
module, so the row is not evidence about the wrapper. That sentence is about spelling. It never
asked the question that decides whether the drop was right: is the name a method of a class
defined in the very module the row was attributed to? If it is, the row *is* evidence about that
module -- someone is calling into the module's own object -- and the reachability rule threw away
a real reader.

This study re-derives E440's attribute population from the live corpus (24,618 rows over 28,258
call rows and 11 confirmed wrappers; the 24,308 in the card text became 24,618 as the tree grew)
and reads two things per row, neither from the other:

* the classes, their methods and the bindable names of the **attributed** module (the wrapper's
  file), indexed once per file;
* the **receiver** spelling at the row's own line in the **caller's** live AST --
  `self`/`cls` in the caller's class, a constructor call, a name the caller binds, a name the
  caller never binds, another expression, or nothing at that line any more.

READINGS. **0 of 24,618 rows name a method of a class in the attributed module.** The reason is
structural, not statistical: all six modules the rows were attributed to
(`_r1191bmb_closeout.py`, `Tools/_r195_rebase_resolve.py`, `Tools/_r1029bmc_close.py`,
`scripts/e110_burncontrol_close.py`, `Tools/_r1390_addendum.py`, `Tools/_r1164bmb_push.py`)
define **no class at all** -- 0 classes, 0 methods across the census. The receivers are ordinary
method names on ordinary objects: `append` 15,464 rows, `write` 4,778, `dump` 2,566, `run` 1,706,
`save` 97, `write_json` 7. By receiver: a name the caller binds 22,746, a constructor call 1,023,
another expression 847, a name the caller never binds 2, `self`/`cls` 0, not-at-that-line 0. The
five remaining wrapper names (`_write_csv`, `_syn_file`, `_judge_lock_acquire`, `apply_close`,
`write_face`) carry no attribute rows at all.

THREE RULES MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.

* **A name fact and a receiver fact are different instruments, and the verdict has to name which
  one fired.** "0 of 24,618" reads like a null result. It is not: it is a census answer. The face
  therefore publishes `classes_defined_across_those_modules` next to the hit count and carries a
  verdict that says *why* the hit is zero
  (`no_attribute_call_row_could_name_a_method_because_the_attributed_modules_define_no_class_at_all`)
  rather than the generic `some_/no_...` pair. Without the census column the same row would have
  been unreadable -- and the guard now refuses any face that claims a hit while the census finds no
  class.
* **The population must be re-derived, not quoted.** The card text says 24,308; the live tree says
  24,618. Publishing the card's number would have made the reproduction check unfalsifiable, so the
  face carries both numbers, `reproduces_e440_attribute_count` is computed from them, and the guard
  re-derives it from its own two fields.
* **A per-name block that lists names with zero rows cannot close against a block that lists only
  graded names.** The first build failed exactly there: `per_name` covered all 11 wrappers while
  `distinct_wrapper_names_graded` counted 6, so the "per_name covers every wrapper name graded"
  leg accused the face of a gap it did not have. The zero-row names are now published separately
  as `wrapper_names_with_no_attribute_rows`, which is the honest shape: they are not graded, they
  are absent.

Face: `results/state_tilt/attrmethod_latest.json` (`ATTRMETHOD-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`no_attribute_call_row_could_name_a_method_because_the_attributed_modules_define_no_class_at_all`;
producer `scripts/e444_attr_method.py` (selftest 36/36, run rc0, check problems=[], verify
problems=[]); S6 leg `attr_call_module_method` (`check`, fast, no corpus walk); smoke leg
`e444 which attribute call names a method of its own module` with a doctored control that must stay
red. Digest `research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1467-e444-attribute-call-method.md`.

## E449 -- a citation of a document means its filename, not its study id

* **A stem is an id, not a citation.** The first build graded all seven dropped `PREREG` pointers
  `cited_in_code_text_only` because the study id (`FUND-QUALITY-P1`) appeared near them. That id is
  in 1,985 closeout lines, handover notes and round reports that have nothing to do with the note.
  Citing the note means naming `research/<STUDY>-P1.md` with its extension. On the tightened rule
  the same seven rows still cite the note (31 distinct `.py` files, 39 citation lines), but two rows
  would have flipped under the loose rule, and the honest shape is to publish the excluded 1,985 as
  a column (`study_id_mentions_excluded_from_the_class`) rather than let them stand as evidence.
  **How:** when a classifier matches a prefix of a name, publish what the prefix also matched.
* **A constant that is assigned and never loaded is not a gate.** All seven declaring files use
  `PREREG` exactly once -- the assignment -- and no opener in 12,197 `.py` files ever takes it. So
  "we froze a prereg" is carried entirely by a string nobody dereferences. The reading that makes
  this legible is the load count, not the presence of the constant: `PREREG = os.path.join(...)` is
  a comment with a name. A study that wants the claim verifiable should hash the note into its own
  output (`prereg_sha16`), because a read that exists only to print a path buys nothing.
* **Narrowing the population must be published, not implicit.** 23 of the 30 dropped compositions
  are not documents (12 not a file, 10 outside research/docs, 1 unresolvable). They sit in
  `out_of_scope_rows` with a reason and the population closes over graded + out-of-scope, so a later
  reader cannot mistake "7" for the size of the question.

Face: `results/state_tilt/deadprereg_latest.json` (`DEADPREREG-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`some_dropped_document_pointers_are_named_in_code_text_but_never_opened`; producer
`scripts/e449_dead_document_pointer.py` (selftest 26/26, run rc0, check problems=[], verify
problems=[], full walk 8 s after replacing `ast.get_source_segment` with a line-table cut); S6 leg
`dead_prereg_pointer` (`check`, fast); smoke leg `e449 which dead prereg pointer is a document no
code ever reads` with a doctored control that must stay red. Digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1468-e449-dead-prereg-pointer.md`.

## E447 -- a base with no writer is harmless only if nobody reads it either (r1469 bm-b)

* **The mirror of a write scan is not "every path in the file".** E446 asked which frozen base has no
  write site; the honest complement asks which has no READ site, and that needs its own vocabulary:
  a call that takes bytes or a listing FROM a path (`open` in a reading mode, `read_text`,
  `read_csv`/`read_parquet`/`read_json` and the other pandas loaders, `np.loadtxt`, `os.listdir`/
  `scandir`/`walk`, `glob`/`rglob`, and the SOURCE argument of copy/move). A call that merely names
  the directory is neither a writer nor a reader and belongs to neither population -- that boundary
  is the whole difference between E446's table and this one. 143 read sites over 133 reader faces,
  against E446's 5,972 writes.
* **A harness name match must be a path, never a basename.** The first build classed 65 of 133
  readers as smoke legs because a bare basename such as `run.py` occurs somewhere in
  `smoke_test.py`. Requiring the repo-relative path or the dotted module path (and the Windows
  backslash spelling for `Tools/*.ps1` wrappers) dropped that to 1 smoke leg and 2 task-referenced
  readers. **How:** any "is this module launched" test that matches a bare filename is measuring the
  harness's prose, not its wiring.
* **A discriminator taken from the population cannot discriminate.** Grading "census vs live
  consumer" from E446's `writer_faces` column gave `face_writing_census = 0`, because that column
  only lists writers that touch the 51 frozen bases; `runnable_script` (any `__main__` guard, which
  is nearly every script here) then swallowed all 43 graded faces. Recomputing "does this module
  publish a face" over the same AST walk (2,013 of the corpus modules do) moved 98 of 133 readers
  into the census class. **How:** a class vocabulary must be derived from the whole corpus, not from
  the rows being graded.

Reading: of E446's 23 bases with no writer, **9 are read by nobody, 11 are still read, and 3 are
backup/rollback directories that are supposed to have none**. Seven are read by code a harness
launches, and four of those seven are the smoke suite itself (`smoke_test.py` opens
`results/etf_book_production/CARD.md`, `results/etf_book_order/latest.json` at two sites and
`results/e79/DOCQUOTES-BASELINE.json`), plus `strategy_scorecard.py` listing `results/g25` and
`trial_labor_w21.py` opening an `overnight_gap_census` leg file. Nothing in the repository would
recreate those artifacts, so the harness depends on bytes no producer owns. `results/p2cal_ext` is
the other shape: 119 sites, all in per-round builder scripts archived under `results/` itself, and
zero of them live.

Face: `results/state_tilt/abandonedread_latest.json` (`ABANDONEDREAD-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`at_least_one_abandoned_base_is_still_read_by_code_a_harness_launches`; producer
`scripts/e447_abandoned_read.py` (selftest 30/30, run rc0, check problems=[], verify problems=[]);
S6 leg `abandoned_read` (`verify`, one corpus AST walk ~60 s); smoke leg `e447 abandoned base read`
with a doctored control that must stay red. Digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1469-e447-abandoned-read.md`.

## E452 -- a truncated reading is not a missing file (r1470 bm-b)

* **Question.** E447 published 7 abandoned bases that code a harness launches still reads. An open on
  a file nobody writes is safe in exactly two worlds: the open is guarded, or the artifact is still
  on disk. Which world is each site in?
* **Answer.** 12 read sites over those 7 bases: **8 guarded, 4 unguarded, and every unguarded target
  exists today** (`every_unguarded_harness_open_still_finds_its_artifact`). The one artifact that is
  gone -- `results/bond_w3a/conn_fuse.json` -- is opened behind an existence test, so its absence
  announces itself instead of raising.
* **The guard ledger is not uniform.** 4 sites sit in a `try`, 4 have an `if os.path.exists(...)`
  that names the same expression with the branch polarity matched, 2 have a negative existence test
  earlier in the enclosing function, 0 use a conditional default. Guard detection is lexical and
  says so: a guard one call away (a wrapper helper) is not credited, and an earlier negative test is
  credited whether or not every path reaches it.
* **The measurement pitfall (the reusable one).** Three sites read
  `os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "t23_census", f"CENSUS-{CUTOFF_PIN}.json")`. The shared resolver
  stops at the f-string head and returns `results/t23_census/CENSUS-`, which is not a path; probing
  it with `os.path.exists` says "gone". That would have published three phantom broken harness opens
  -- in the smoke-suite family that natural experiment is exactly the one this card exists for.
  **A resolved value that came from a truncated composition must not be probed; publish it as
  unresolved, or complete it and publish the provenance.** This face completes it from the module
  constants and prints `resolution=completed_fstring` beside `shared_resolver_path`, so a completed
  reading is never mistaken for a shared one; 9 sites stayed `shared_resolver`, 0 unresolved.
* **Population honesty.** E447 counted 7 bases read by a live consumer; the live re-walk finds 7 but
  one of them (`results/overnight_gap_census`) has no site whose reader is live under today's scan,
  so it carries a row with zero sites and is named in
  `summary.bases_where_e447_live_reader_is_not_live_now` rather than silently dropped.
* **A guard is not a producer.** All 8 guarded sites still point at bytes no producer owns. The
  reading is "a missing artifact would be announced", not "the harness can be fixed by adding a
  producer" -- the fix decision belongs to the lane host that owns each base.

Face: `results/state_tilt/abandonedguard_latest.json` (`ABANDONEDGUARD-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`every_unguarded_harness_open_still_finds_its_artifact`; producer
`scripts/e452_abandoned_guard.py` (selftest 27/27, run rc0, check problems=[], verify problems=[]);
S6 leg `abandoned_guard` (`verify`, one corpus walk ~60 s); smoke leg `e452 abandoned base harness
guard` with a doctored control that must stay red. Digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1470-e452-abandoned-guard.md`.

## E453 -- mtime age cannot exceed the age of the checkout that set it (r1471.1 bm-b)

* **Question.** E452 left 11 harness read sites under an abandoned base whose artifact is still on
  disk, and said the guard only announces *absence*. Is any of those targets stale -- and does the
  code that reads it check an age at all?
* **Answer, and the trap that answers it.** Ages 8..20 days, threshold 180, so all 11 come back
  `fresh_artifact` -- and that reading is worthless here, on purpose. The published floor block
  shows why: **29,133 files share the mtime date 2026-10-17** (58,178 walked, 20 distinct dates,
  oldest 2026-10-16). A checkout stamps every file with the materialisation moment, so an
  mtime-derived age is capped at 21 days on this tree no matter how old the content is. Verdict is
  therefore not "fresh" but
  `mtime_age_cannot_exceed_the_checkout_floor_so_staleness_is_not_identifiable_here_and_every_fresh_reading_is_an_artifact_of_materialisation`.
* **The reusable law.** Before any age/freshness claim from filesystem mtimes, measure the floor:
  the oldest mtime in the tree and the modal mtime date with its count. If
  `max_identifiable_age_days < threshold`, the measurement is **not identifiable** and a "fresh"
  result must be published as an artefact of materialisation, not as evidence. A staleness check
  that returns green on a freshly-cloned tree is measuring `git clone`, not the pipeline. The
  threshold is a named constant (`STALE_DAYS = 180`) fixed before the data, so it cannot be tuned to
  the answer.
* **What is still measured and true.** The age-check half of the question does not depend on mtime:
  6 of 11 reading scopes read the clock, 4 name a max-age/staleness constant or argument, 0 compare
  an `st_mtime`, and every site's enclosing function was located and published. Those forms are
  incidental hygiene, not freshness gates: a clock read inside a reader is not a check that the
  bytes are current.
* **Two aggregators, published apart.** The class table (fresh/stale-checked/stale-bare) and the
  identifiability block are separate; the verdict is computed from both and the identifiability arm
  takes precedence, so a future tree with a genuinely old floor will produce the ordinary verdict
  without any code change. The `check` leg refuses a verdict that disagrees with the floor and
  refuses any target that measures older than the floor it publishes.
* **Boundary.** Six of the seven E452 bases contributed sites; the row with no present target is
  dropped rather than carried as a zero row, and `bases_graded=6` says so. Nothing here decides
  whether a stale artifact should be deleted -- it decides whether anyone would notice.

Face: `results/state_tilt/abandonedstale_latest.json` (`ABANDONEDSTALE-<cutoff>.json`); producer
`scripts/e453_abandoned_stale.py` (selftest 25/25, run rc0, check problems=[], verify problems=[]);
smoke leg `e453 abandoned base target staleness` with a doctored control that must stay red. Digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1471-e453-abandoned-stale.md`.

## E454 -- a site address that is a line number in a file that grows every round is not an address (r1471 bm-b)

* **Question.** A census publishes each read site as `file:line` and its `verify` re-walks the tree
  and requires that exact string to still be there. What happens to a face whose only growing member
  is the suite itself?
* **Answer.** It goes red for reasons that have nothing to do with the defect it measures. E398
  published 216 read sites; `smoke_test.py` gained legs in three rounds and the same face now
  re-derives 222 sites and 7 of its published addresses resolve to nothing. The suite leg reported
  `smoke_test.py:16977: the site is gone` -- a site that still exists, six thousand lines above where
  it used to be. **Nothing about the pointer convention changed; only the line numbers did.**
* **The durable key.** A site's identity is its own text: `(file, kind, expr)` plus the occurrence
  index of that exact `(kind, expr)` inside that file. `file:line` stays in the face for humans, and
  `anchor` becomes what `verify` matches on. An address that moved is then a published count
  (`address moves=N`) instead of a problem, and the checks that matter -- the expression, the class,
  the guard -- still run on the live row.
* **How to apply.** Any face that indexes sites by line number must either (a) publish a
  content-anchored key beside the human address and verify on the key, or (b) stop verifying
  addresses at all and verify derived classifications only. Applies to every census in this repo
  whose corpus includes `smoke_test.py`, the round reports, or any append-only file -- which is most
  of them. Consequence for the round: 9 of the 10 standing suite FAILs this window were the
  "published summary does not re-derive from the live tree" class, and the repair is a republish from
  the producer, never a loosened leg.

Face: `results/state_tilt/latestfamily_latest.json`; producer `scripts/e398_latest_family.py`
(`verify problems=[] (address moves=0)`). Republished in the same window: WRONGSIDE, REFRESHSIGNAL,
UNFLOORED, READERTIERS, FRESHAIM, FACEAGE, UNSTAMPABLE, BASENAMECENSUS, SHADOWFACE, DIRISFACE.

## E450 -- a name is not a type, and the name arm of a misattribution question is a coincidence generator (r1475 bm-b)

E444 answered the wrapper side of E440's 24,308 dropped attribute call rows: the six modules those
rows were attributed to define zero classes, so no row could name a method there. The caller side
was never read -- if the receiver is a name the caller binds, the class it names a method of is
usually defined in the caller's own module, and that row is a real reader filed under the wrong
module.

* **Question.** Of the rows whose receiver is a caller-bound name or a constructor call made in the
  caller (23,982 of 24,831 attribute rows), how many name a method that a class defined in the
  **caller's** file carries -- and how many have a receiver that actually **is** that class?
* **Two arms, published separately.** *Name*: the method name appears among the methods of some
  class defined in the caller's file -- 26 rows (0.11%). *Binding*: the receiver is that class,
  assigned a call to a local class (or the receiver is that constructor call) which carries the
  name -- 13 rows (0.05%).
* **The reading.** The 13-row gap is not scattered noise: it is exactly the whole of
  `Tools/pool_worker.py`, the single largest name-hit module (13 name hits, **0** binding hits).
  The two modules that do contribute are unambiguous and spot-read in source:
  `fwd = Forward(...) -> fwd.run(...)` (plus `f0..f5`) in `scripts/etf_book_forward.py` (11), and
  `policy = TinyPolicy(...) -> policy.save(...)` in `scripts/alphagen_rl_p1.py` (2). So the name
  index misattributed nothing resembling a population of readers; it missed 13 rows in two files.
* **What the binding block says about the rest.** 6,875 rows bind the receiver to a call that is
  not a local class, 11,685 bind it to something that is not a call at all, 4,375 never assign it
  here (parameter / import / loop target), 1,026 are constructor rows. A receiver is therefore
  almost never a local object in this corpus, which is the honest scope of the finding.
* **The pin, and why it is a rule.** The face re-derives E444's population live and pins itself to
  E444's published receiver distribution under E455's growth rule: no kind may lose rows, and
  E444's own distribution must rebuild its published total. Measured here: 24,831 vs E444's 24,618
  (**+213**), entirely `bound` +210 and `ctor` +3 while the other four kinds are byte-identical
  (2 / 847 / 0 / 0) -- growth in the two in-scope kinds and no classifier drift, verdict
  `growth_only_superset`. Two builds nine minutes apart read 24,823 and 24,831: the tree grows
  while you measure it.
* **The pit, on its own round.** The first `verify` compared the published summary with a fresh
  reading by exact equality -- the defect E455 was carded for, committed by the round after the fix
  landed. `verify` now hands both payloads to `scripts/growth_tolerance.py` with the demographic
  (receiver kind, binding, caller kind) as row identity and the claim (`name_hit`, `binding_hit`)
  as the class, so growth is reported and only a lost cell, a shrunk count or a flipped claim
  refuses.
* **How to apply.** Any question of the form "did the index misattribute readers to the wrong
  module?" must publish the **name arm and the binding arm separately**, because the name arm is
  inflated by ordinary method-name collisions -- here, 100% of one module's hits. A census that
  answers "does X name Y" without asking "is the receiver Y" is a lower bound wearing an answer's
  clothes. Sibling rule for the pin: a face that re-derives a growing population must assert
  *direction* (no losses, no flips), never equality, or it re-reds one round after every republish.

Face: `results/state_tilt/callerclass_latest.json` (+ `CALLERCLASS-<cutoff>.json`); producer
`scripts/e450_caller_class.py` (selftest 43/43, run rc0, check problems=0, verify problems=[]);
digest `research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1475-e450-caller-class.md`.

## E451 -- a study's claim to follow a prereg is prose unless a face carries its digest (r1477 bm-b)

* **Question.** E449 published seven research notes that a study script names through a `PREREG`
  constant, that code text cites by filename, and that **no opener in the corpus ever opens** -- the
  constant is assigned once and never read again. If the note constrains the study, some artifact
  the study publishes should be tieable to the note's exact bytes. Which studies publish a digest of
  the note they claim to follow?
* **Population, re-derived not inherited.** The seven notes are E449's rows; for each one the naming
  set is every `.py` in the corpus (12,210 walked) whose text carries the note basename -- 32 naming
  sites over 31 distinct files, matching E449's own 31. Of those, 28 publish at least one string
  literal that resolves under `results/`; 11 are the study's **own** producer (the file whose
  basename carries the study slug, e.g. `scripts/fund_divlowvol_p1.py` for `FUND-DIVLOWVOL-P1`) and
  the other 17 are lane receipts and shared modules that merely name the note. Studies are graded on
  their own producer's faces (24 probed), with every naming producer's faces published beside it
  (84 probed, 10 targets absent from disk).
* **The reading, and it is a zero.** No study publishes a digest of its prereg: 0 faces carry the
  note's sha256, 0 carry a hex prefix of at least 12 characters, 0 carry a keyed ISO as-of. Verdict
  `no_study_publishes_a_digest_of_the_prereg_note_it_names`; all seven are
  `note_named_but_no_digest`, none falls back to `note_not_named_by_its_own_producer`.
* **The near miss is the real finding.** 65 faces name a prereg field or the study stem and carry no
  digest (23 of them written by an own producer). Two of the seven studies record their freeze the
  same way, in prose: `prereg_state = "FROZEN v1.0 (2026-10-03 bm-b r610 five-condition freeze
  window)"` in `results/fund_divlowvol_p1/probe.json`, and `prereg = "research/FUND-DIVLOWVOL-P1.md
  (DRAFT-NOT-FROZEN)"` in `results/_fund_divlowvol_p1_transfer_probe.json` -- **the same note, a
  frozen state in one face and an unfrozen state in another, and neither string lets a reader check
  either claim.** That is what a claim without a digest costs: two artifacts of one study disagree
  about the state of the document that is supposed to bind it, and no machine can adjudicate.
* **The law.** A "frozen prereg" is machine-checkable only if the producer's own face carries
  `prereg_sha256` (the note bytes, or a prefix of at least 12 hex chars) or a keyed ISO
  `prereg_as_of`. A date inside a sentence is not a pin: it cannot be keyed on, it does not name
  bytes, and it drifts from the note silently. Publish prose freeze strings as claims, never count
  them as pins.
* **How to apply.** Before quoting "our prereg says X", ask the face that publishes the numbers for
  `prereg_sha256`/`prereg_as_of`; if it is absent, the tie is prose and the note may have been
  edited since the run. Symmetrically, when a study records a freeze, write the digest of the bytes
  it froze, so a later edit of the note is visible instead of invisible. The measurement is cheap
  (one corpus walk plus 84 face loads, 3.8 s) and belongs beside any freeze gate.

Face: `results/state_tilt/prereghash_latest.json` (+ `PREREGHASH-<cutoff>.json`), verdict
`no_study_publishes_a_digest_of_the_prereg_note_it_names`; producer
`scripts/e451_prereg_digest.py` (selftest 30/30, run rc0, check problems=[], verify problems=[]);
S6 leg `prereg_digest` (`verify`, one corpus walk, 3.8 s); smoke leg `e451 which study that names a
prereg note publishes a digest of it` with a doctored control that must stay red. Digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1477-e451-prereg-digest.md`.

## E456 -- a zero is a reading only with a control: the cross-module half of an attribute census (r1478 bm-b)

* **Question.** E450 graded the caller side of E444's 24,831 attribute call rows and published 6,875
  whose receiver is a name bound to a call to something that is **not** a class the caller defines.
  If the receiver's class exists, it came from elsewhere. Resolve each callee through the caller's
  own imports to a module in this repository, index that module's classes and methods, and count the
  rows that name a method the imported class carries.
* **Population, inherited not re-derived.** E450's own `graded_rows()` was extracted from its
  `build()` and filtered to the cross-module binding, so a second derivation cannot disagree about
  who is in scope: 6,898 rows over 3,499 corpus sources (E450 arm 6,875, delta +23, growth-only
  superset). E450's `check` and `selftest 46/46` still pass after the refactor.
* **The reading is a zero.** 0 of 6,898 callees resolve to a class defined in an in-repo module, so
  0 rows name a method such a class carries. Verdict
  `no_row_callee_resolves_to_a_class_defined_in_this_repository`.
* **The zero is priced by mechanism.** Residue is not one bucket: builtin 3,495 (50.7%, `open()`
  dominates), local factory 2,238, import resolving outside this repository 928, name not
  imported/bound/local 113, imported name is a function 59, call target not a plain/qualified name
  54, attribute of an imported object 10, module defines no such name 1. 1,000 rows did travel
  through an import (853 module-level, 137 module-level aliased, 6 function-level, 2 function-level
  aliased) and none named a class.
* **Why the zero is measured.** The face publishes a resolver control: 36 of 69,562 corpus-wide
  assignments whose value is a call to a plain or qualified name do resolve to an in-repo class
  (`ExitConfig`/`ExitState`/`FeeSchedule`, harvested by `engine/backtester.py` and
  `monitor/build_status.py`). An instrument that never fires cannot publish a zero, and the tally
  refuses a face whose control reads 0.
* **Four rules this cost.** (1) A coarse residue bucket destroys the finding: folding builtins, local
  factories and untraceable imports into "not imported" left one story (5,846) where the split says
  half the population is `open()`. (2) A dotted-only import resolver resolves nothing in a tree that
  imports siblings by bare name; try both spellings and publish ambiguity as ambiguity. (3) A method
  name is not a module-level name: reading the whole AST for "functions defined here" grades an
  import of a method as "imported a function". (4) The import form belongs to the import that was
  involved, not to the one that succeeded -- requiring a form only on hits made the face refuse the
  928 outside-tree rows that are the largest traceable block.
* **Wiring.** `scripts/e456_import_class.py` (run / check 0 / verify 0 / selftest 42/42); S6 leg
  `import_class`; smoke leg with a doctored control that must stay red (face restored
  byte-identical); digest `research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1478-e456-import-class.md`.

## E459 -- a residue of out-of-tree modules is not a zero: the standard-library classes behind an import census (r1480 bm-b)

* **Question.** E456 resolved the cross-module half of E444's attribute-call rows and found 928 whose
  callee module has no file in this repository. Those are not unmeasured rows: the module name is a
  handle the instrument can use without a network, because the interpreter already has the module.
  Resolve the name through the module table, look the class up by the name the import form carried,
  and count the rows that name a method that class carries.
* **The reading.** Of 960 rows on this residue (E456's 928, growth-only superset +32), **960/960
  import** and **17 name a class of the kind the import form named** (1.8%); of those 17, **4 carry
  the method the row calls** (`io.StringIO.write`, 23.5% of what was looked up, 0.42% of the block).
* **The finding is in the split, not in the rate.** 943 of the 960 are *attributes that exist and are
  not classes* -- `io.open` (804), `subprocess.run` (25), `numpy.isfinite` (24), `asarray` (13),
  `tempfile.mkdtemp` (13). Folding "not a class" into "does not resolve" would have published a
  residue of 960 and said the standard library was the untraceable part, when in fact the untraceable
  part is empty (0 not importable, 0 imports that raised): the block is **factory functions**, and no
  method index can grade a factory. Only 17 rows are the population E450's name index could have got
  wrong.
* **The form is the predictor.** Module-level imports carry 863 of the rows and 8 of the classes (4
  hits); module-level aliased 83 / 7 / 0; function-level 13 / 1 / 0; function-level aliased 1 / 1 / 0.
  A from-import names a class, a module-qualified call names whatever attribute the caller wrote -- so
  the import form that dominates the count is the form that carries the least class identity.
* **Four rules this cost.** (1) A residue is a reading only if you resolve it: "the module is not in
  the tree" is a statement about the tree, not about the module. (2) Split *attribute absent* from
  *attribute present but not a class*: the first is a name-index gap, the second is a factory, and
  merging them makes the 98% invisible. (3) `find_spec` before `import_module`: "no such module" and
  "the module raised" are different findings and the second is not the first's residue. (4) A class
  found is not a method hit -- the two readings are published separately, and the second is only
  meaningful inside the first.
* **Wiring.** `scripts/e459_stdlib_class.py` (run rc0 / verify clean / selftest 15/15); face
  `results/state_tilt/stdlibclass_latest.json` + `STDLIBCLASS-<cutoff>.json` + `stdlibclass_by_module_
  <cutoff>.csv`; S6 leg `stdlib_class` (re-derives the tallies, then re-resolves the published hits
  and residues against the live module table, 0.05 s); digest
  `research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1480-e459-stdlib-class.md`. No smoke leg this round (stated, not
  implied): the chain leg is the live gate.

## E458 -- a face can be addressed by its file name and still not say which study wrote it (r1482 bm-b)

* **Question.** E451 found that no study publishes a digest of the prereg note it names, and that the
  note is reachable only through prose freeze strings. A digest presupposes something earlier: a
  consumer holding a face must be able to tell *which* study it belongs to without opening the
  producer. Ask every face a study producer writes whether its payload carries a machine-readable
  identity -- a card id (`E4xx`), a study id (`XXX-P1`) or a prereg note path -- in a field a reader
  can key on, and whether that identity resolves to a file or a pool card that exists.
* **The reading.** 538 faces graded against the 12,130-source corpus by producer-first attribution:
  **526 carry a machine-readable identity** (all three kinds seen: card id, study id, prereg path),
  **2 carry one only inside a prose field**, **10 carry none at all**, 0 unreadable, and **0
  declarations fail to resolve** (6 faces carry a declaration that does not resolve to a file or card,
  and those are published per row rather than folded into the tally).
* **The split is the finding, not the 97.8%.** The 12 that are not machine-readable are 7 distinct
  producers: `BANDDONORCHOICE`/`BANDFLOOR`/`BANDSCREENBUDGET`/`CORPUSPIN`/`FACEVINTAGE`/
  `unreadstatus_latest` carry no identity whatsoever (6 of the 10 rows are the same 5 studies' dated
  + `_latest` twins, so a study-level count is 6, not 10), while `BANDSTRADDLESWEEP` names its card
  twice inside `summary.hits` -- parseable text, prose field, therefore *not* a keyable identity
  under a frozen field-name vocabulary. Merging prose-only into machine-readable would have reported
  528 and hidden the one shape E451 is about.
* **Three rules this cost.** (1) **Population comes from producers, never from a hand list**: a face
  belongs to a producer when the producer's source carries the face name as a constant, a dated
  prefix template, or the dated sibling, with both sides normalised (lowercase, drop `.json`, drop a
  trailing date, drop `_latest`) -- so `importclass_latest.json` and `IMPORTCLASS-2026-11-04.json` are
  one study's two faces and are graded as two rows. (2) **A mention of another study is not this
  face's identity**: a study id inside a long value (a face path in somebody else's row, a script
  name) is discounted -- 5,466 substring mentions on 390 faces -- and only counts when the field
  itself is named like an identity; the discounted set is sampled in the face so the classifier
  change is a measurement and not a silent rewrite. (3) **The unattributed residue is published, not
  zeroed**: 39 faces under `results/state_tilt` that no `scripts/eNNN_*.py` names sit outside the
  graded population and are reported as a count with samples rather than as carrying or lacking.
* **Wiring.** `scripts/e458_face_identity.py` (run rc0 / check clean / selftest 24/24); faces
  `results/state_tilt/faceidentity_latest.json` + `FACEIDENTITY-2026-11-06.json`; S6 leg
  `face_identity` (re-derives the tallies and re-resolves the published declarations against the live
  tree, 0.06 s); smoke leg `e458 does a study face declare a machine-readable identity (r1482 bm-b)`
  + `scripts/run_e458_smoke_leg.py` (standalone 1/1, and the leg reds on a doctored copy that promotes
  a no-identity row into the machine-readable class); digest
  `research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1482-e458-face-identity.md`.

## E461 -- a declaration nobody reads is a label: measure the link, and split the generic key names out (r1483 bm-b)

* **Question.** E458 published that 526 of 538 study faces declare a machine-readable identity and
  that every declaration resolves. Resolving is not reading. Ask, for every graded face, whether a
  source *other than its own producer* names the face **and** reads a field the face declares; and,
  separately, whether the joining source also carries the declared value as its own literal. Then ask
  the same question of the vocabulary itself: of the 15 field names E458 froze, which are ever read?
* **The reading.** 526 faces graded over 8,209 `.py` sources (own outputs excluded). **389 are named
  by a source that reads a declared field**, **12 are joined by a source that also carries the
  declared value as an exact string constant**, **130 are named only by their own producer**, **1 is
  named by a consumer that reads none of its fields**, **6 are named by nobody**. Of the 15 identity
  field names, **7 are never read by any source** -- and they are exactly the shape-named ones
  (`card_id`, `study_id`, `prereg_path` plus `prereg_note`, `pinned_note`, `source_card`,
  `source_cards`): readers key on the *generic* names (`study`, `card`), never on the vocabulary that
  gives the shape its precision.
* **Rule 1: a file-level conjunction is not a link.** "Some file names this face and some file reads
  `study`" is one conjunction over an entire source, and a census reader satisfies it for every face
  it walks. 385 of the 389 joins come from a single source (`smoke_test.py`) that names >10 faces;
  the **face-specific** join count is **4**. The breadth of the joining source (`joined_breadth`) is
  published on every row so the two shapes cannot be read as one number.
* **Rule 2: exact literal is not substring.** `E452` occurs twice in `smoke_test.py` but never as a
  compared literal -- only inside leg labels -- so a "value appears somewhere in the source" test
  reports a join that the code does not make. The value join is graded on string constants that
  appear **exactly**, which is why it reads 12 and not 389. `smoke_test.py` *does* read
  `_doc.get("study") == "E229"` for the legs that carry the exact literal; both shapes are real and
  are published apart.
* **Rule 3: generic key names inflate the census.** The vocabulary shares three names with ordinary
  payload keys (`id`, `pin`, `pid`). `id` alone carries **1,125 read sites across 895 files**
  (`Money0923/quant/arena.py` et al) that have nothing to do with a study identity. Identity-named
  read sites are **110**; ambiguous-named are **1,242**. Folding them together would let "every field
  is read" pass on the strength of `d["id"]`.
* **Wiring.** `scripts/e461_identity_consumers.py` (run rc0 / verify problems=[] / check clean /
  **selftest 24/24**); faces `results/state_tilt/identityconsumers_latest.json` +
  `IDENTITYCONSUMERS-2026-11-06.json`; S6 leg `identity_consumers` (re-derives the tallies from the
  published rows); smoke leg `e461 does a consumer read the identity a face declares (r1483 bm-b)` +
  `scripts/run_e461_smoke_leg.py` (standalone 1/1, red on a copy that promotes an unread face into
  the joined class); digest `research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1483-e461-identity-consumers.md`.
* **Bound published, not claimed.** Static only: a consumer that reaches the field through a computed
  key is invisible; a consumer that compares against a constant imported from elsewhere counts as a
  field join, not a value join; a name composed from parts is not matched (E458's bound, inherited).
  Read-vs-write is decided by AST context, not data flow.

### E462 -- a face's identity is written in a dialect almost nobody speaks, and the two faces that speak it contradict themselves (r1485 bm-b)

E461 closed the vocabulary side of the identity question: 15 frozen identity field names, 7 read by
no source at all, and the never-read ones are exactly the shape-named ones (`card_id`, `study_id`,
`prereg_path`, `prereg_note`, `pinned_note`, `source_card`, `source_cards`). The natural next
sentence -- "so faces must be writing their identities in a dead dialect" -- is a sentence nobody
had measured. This study asks it of the 526 graded faces E461 used, not of the vocabulary:

* **The dialect is almost unwritten.** 617 declared field instances over 526 faces, **2** of them in
  a name no source reads. 524 faces speak only names a source reads, **2 are redundant** (a
  never-read name beside a read one), **0 are silent**. Only three distinct names are ever declared
  on any face: `card`, `study`, `source_study`. The 15-name vocabulary is much wider than the
  dialect the corpus actually writes.
* **Both redundant faces contradict themselves.** `results/state_tilt/SELFRES-2026-10-29.json` and
  its `selfres_latest.json` twin declare `source_study: "E252"` beside `study: "E253"`. A second
  voice naming a *different* study is the worst shape of a dead dialect: nothing reads it, so no
  gate can ever see the disagreement. A redundant declaration is only harmless when it agrees.
* **A redundant voice is harmless only when it agrees -- and a *read* voice can disagree too.**
  `NAMERESOLVE-2026-11-04.json` declares `card: "E413"` beside `study: "E421"` (both names
  read, so a `card` reader joins the face to E413 and a `study` reader to E421, with nothing
  arbitrating), while `SELFRES-2026-10-29.json` declares `source_study: "E252"` beside
  `study: "E253"` (one voice dead, so the disagreement was invisible to every gate). 89 of 526
  faces declare both `card` and `study`; 4 faces (2 file pairs) carry more than one identity
  value. Measuring agreement is a column of its own, not a by-product of measuring which names
  are read.
* **Join exposure is the price of the read names.** 389 faces are joined today by a consumer keying
  on a read name (carried from E461's rows, 0 absent), so dropping the spoken name would unjoin all
  389. The silent dialect is not an extra voice; it is the only voice on the faces that have none.
* **Rule 1: a name outside a frozen vocabulary is not a never-read name until it is measured.** The
  first build classified `source_study` as never-read by construction (it is simply absent from
  E458's 15-name list), which would have published "2 faces write in a dead dialect" on the back of
  a lookup miss. The census was widened to `vocabulary ∪ declared names`; `source_study` was then
  measured at 0 read sites, so the claim survives -- but now it survives as a measurement. The
  payload carries `fields_outside_the_frozen_vocabulary` and a per-face count so the distinction can
  never be silent again (E207/E208 family: a classifier that accepts a name it never looked at).
* **Rule 2: a scanner must exclude itself and its predecessor.** This family is the only thing in the
  repo that reads identity field names *as* field names, so every instrument in it would vote for
  the dialect it studies. E462 excludes `e461_`/`e462_`/`run_e461`/`run_e462` and both faces, and
  publishes `field_census_per_e461` plus `fields_whose_read_status_disagrees_with_e461` (empty this
  round) rather than silently re-deriving a peer's counts.
* **Wiring.** `scripts/e462_identity_dialect.py` (run rc0 / verify problems=[] / check problems=[] /
  **selftest 22/22**); faces `results/state_tilt/identitydialect_latest.json` +
  `IDENTITYDIALECT-2026-11-06.json`; S6 leg `identity_dialect`; smoke leg `e462 is a face's identity
  written in a dialect anyone reads (r1485 bm-b)` + `scripts/run_e462_smoke_leg.py` (red on a copy
  that recasts a read-only face as redundant); digest
  `research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1485-e462-identity-dialect.md`.
* **Bound published, not claimed.** Static only: a name reached through a composed key would be
  counted never-read (inflating the silent count, which is 0 here, so the bound costs nothing);
  contradiction compares declared values as strings, so a case/spacing difference reads as a
  contradiction and must be read from the row.

## E463 -- when two read names disagree a face joins two studies, and the only consumer is the suite (r1486 bm-b)

**Where it came from.** E462 closed with "4 faces (2 file pairs) carry more than one identity value
and 89 of 526 declare both `card` and `study`", and left open which study a consumer actually ends
up bound to. This card answers it on the consumer side.

**Law.** `names_read -> binds_to` is not a join, it is a *choice* the payload never states. Bind
every non-producer consumer of the face to the value the face declares **under the name that
consumer reads**, and then ask how many distinct studies one face is bound to:

* `NAMERESOLVE-2026-11-04.json` declares `card: E413` beside `study: E421` and `smoke_test.py` reads
  both, so one consumer holds two bindings at once. Nothing arbitrates; both lookups succeed and the
  leg passes for the wrong reason.
* `SELFRES-2026-10-29.json` declares `source_study: E252` beside `study: E253`, but the second voice
  is read by nobody (E462), so every consumer binds E253. **A never-read voice is a disagreement no
  consumer can reach** -- E462's dialect hazard, priced here at zero on the consumer side.
* 87 of the 89 both-name faces agree, so the synonym shape is a convention and the 4 disagreeing
  faces are a **writer** defect: one producer wrote two labels and meant one study. Neither card's
  producer names the face, so the join exists only in field names.

**Numbers.** 4 multi-value faces, 2 read-voice disagreements (+2 latest twins), 4 consumers total
(one per face, all `smoke_test.py`), `card` 2 / `study` 4 / `source_study` 0, 2 both-name consumers,
2 faces bound to two studies, 0 of 4 cards whose producer names the face.

**Pits.**

* **A fixture that hand-keys the index tests the key, not the code.** Fixture face
  `SPLIT-2026-11-06.json` normalises to stem `split` (`norm_stem` strips the date tail); keying the
  fixture corpus on `split20261106` failed four legs that never met their own selector.
* **A breadth map built over the whole corpus cannot be handed a corpus subset** -- `by_rel[rel]`
  raises `KeyError` instead of returning "no consumers". Cut both sides from the same corpus.
* **A gate is proven by a consistent face, not a convenient one.** Two fixture summaries were
  internally inconsistent (split count > 0 beside rows binding one study; per-name total that did
  not add), so "gate accepts a consistent face" failed for the fixture's arithmetic -- the gate was
  working on the wrong patient.

**Wiring.** `scripts/e463_identity_split.py` (run rc0 / verify problems=[] / check problems=[] /
**selftest 21/21**); faces `results/state_tilt/identitysplit_latest.json` +
`IDENTITYSPLIT-2026-11-06.json`; S6 leg `identity_split`; smoke leg
`e463 a face with two read names binds two studies (r1486 bm-b)` +
`scripts/run_e463_smoke_leg.py`; digest
`research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1486-e463-identity-split.md`; pool E463 done, E464 seeded.

**Bound.** Static only: a consumer reaching a name through a composed key is invisible, and a
consumer that hard-codes a study id is counted in `values_carried` rather than `binds_to`. Producer
detection for a card is a filename prefix or an equal literal, so a producer naming its card only in
prose is missed -- which is why `card_producers` is published beside the zero.

## E464 -- a producer's intent is not in the payload: one constant plus one carried value is a provenance, not a second identity (r1487 bm-b)

**Question.** E463 showed the only consumer of the multi-value faces is the suite, so the two voices
come from one producer that holds one intention and two labels. E464 asks the producer itself: which
identity do its own module constants, literals and carried values say it meant?

**Method.** Population is the parent face's 4 multi-value rows; the producers are that face's own
producer list, re-measured against the live `.py` corpus. Three separate measurements per producer:
**W** does it write this face (path expressions of open-for-write / `write_text` calls expanded
through module assignments and tuple for-loops into face stems), **K** what kind of expression the
producer writes under each identity key (literal / resolved module constant / call-or-subscript =
carried), **M** whether the declared value equals the payload value or only carries it as a slug
prefix (`E413` -> `E413-DOES-THE-...`).

**Result.** 4 faces, 2 stems, 6 named producers: 4 write the face, 2 do not (E462's producer list
contains `e254_band_exponent_inside_cell.py`, which merely names `SELFRES-2026-10-29.json` and
writes its own face). Among the 4 writers: `e421` writes **both** voices itself (card E413 and study
E421, both only as slug prefixes -- 4 of 4 matching votes are prefix-only), while `e253` writes
`study = STUDY ("E253")` and takes `source_study` straight from the upstream payload
(`src.get("study")`) -- **one declaration plus one carried provenance value**.

**The finding that changes the parent's frame.** The faces carry 10 identity-key instances over 3
names (`card`, `study`, `source_study`), and **2 of 4 faces carry an identity key E462 never graded**
(`source_study` on both NAMERESOLVE faces = `E406_blob_vs_tree_readers`). The E462/E463 "two names"
census saw a face with three voices and graded two. 4 of 4 faces also carry a pointer key
(`source_face`), which is a path not an identity: on the same face the pointer is the only exact
match while every study voice is a slug, so a distance-based identity matcher would prefer the
pointer to the card.

**Pits.**
* **A slug is not a mismatch, but it is not equality either.** All four `E413`/`E421` votes are
  `prefixed`, zero `exact`. Publishing them merged would report "the producer declares the payload
  value" when it declares a longer label; the two are published apart.
* **A pointer key read as an identity inflates the census.** With `source_face` in the identity
  vocabulary the first run reported 14 identity instances and 4 faces writing an identity key the
  payload does not carry; splitting pointers out dropped it to 10 and 0. A path is not a study id.
* **A producer name in a parent face is a claim, not a measurement.** Two of six named producers
  write a different face; `writes_this_face` re-measures it and the residue is published.
* **`face_stem` must slice the basename before stripping the `%s` placeholder.** `results/x/SELFRES-%s.json`
  normalised to `results/x/selfress` in the first pass (`norm_stem` gives the same `selfress`), so
  every writer looked like a non-writer and all four faces read "no writer". Slice first.

**Numbers.** 4 multi-value faces / 2 stems; 6 producers named, 4 write, 2 do not; intent among
writers: both-voices 2, one+carried 2, one-only 0, nothing-declared 0; payload identity keys
`card`/`study`/`source_study` over 10 instances; 2 of 4 faces carry a parent-ungraded identity key;
4 of 4 carry a pointer key; 10 producer instances write a pointer key.

**Wiring.** `scripts/e464_producer_intent.py` (run rc0 / verify problems=[] / check problems=[] /
selftest 39/39); faces `results/state_tilt/producerintent_latest.json` +
`PRODUCERINTENT-2026-11-06.json`; S6 leg `producer_intent`; smoke leg
`e464 which identity a producer intends when it writes two names (r1487 bm-b)` +
`scripts/run_e464_smoke_leg.py` (red-proved on a doctored face, then restored byte-identical);
digest `research/digests/DIGEST-20261106-r1487-e464-producer-intent.md`; pool E464 done, E465 seeded.

**Bound.** The producer list is the parent's; this study can refute a listed producer but cannot
discover one the parent never listed. A writer is recognised only through path expressions resolved
through module assignments and tuple loops -- a path built by a function call or dict lookup is
published as a non-writer. Intent is read from dict literals and constant-key subscripts only.

**How to apply.** Before treating two identity fields on one face as two claims, read the producer:
a key whose value is a call (`payload.get(...)`) is provenance being forwarded, and a key whose
value is a module constant is the only place the producer actually declares what it is. Grade the
payload's own identity keys rather than a fixed pair, and publish pointer keys separately, or the
census undercounts voices and overcounts disagreements.

## E465 -- a name test's optimism is the method names of modules that never import the function (r1488 bm-b)

**Where it came from.** E450's name arm read 26 hits and the single largest block of them (13, all
`Tools/pool_worker.py`) carried zero rows where the receiver was that module's own class. The
suspicion was a wrapper name colliding with an unrelated class's method name; nobody had measured
how common that is outside the eleven graded wrappers.

**Law.** Population = every module-level function the tree defines (the tree itself, not a curated
family). For each name: `C` = other modules that define a class carrying a method of that name;
